a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectTitle: Digital Community Engagement Accelerator for student learning and socio-economic impact
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectTags: Community development |Digital content, technologies and practices|Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectLevel2Label: Partnerships for cooperation and exchanges of practices
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectDescriptionBackground: The COVID-19 pandemic showed us that many activities could successfully move online. We adapted to working remotely, teaching virtually, and even connecting socially through digital tools. Digitalization became a part of everyday life, and universities were no exception. But beyond research and teaching, universities also had a third mission: to act as a bridge between academia and society, using their expertise to address social and economic challenges.The project aimed to combine these two topics: digitalization and the third mission of universities. Drawing inspiration from business accelerators, DICE developed a program to guide university educators in designing digital CE courses. Traditional CE had restrictions, whereas digital tools offered a broader scope—reaching across borders and involving groups that were previously difficult to access. Still, many educators struggled with where to start. They often lacked the awareness, structure, and support needed to take their courses digital. DICE responded to this by offering a structured, step-by-step program to make digital CE more accessible and impactful.
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The DICE project aimed to strengthen the third mission of universitis, their engagement with society, while at the same time fostering digitalisation in higher education. Our goal was to bring community engagement into the online environment through the development of the DICE Accelerator, an innovative online platform that guides educators step by step in creating or enhancing their courses with digital community engagement components.
The Accelerator was built upon the Value Maps framework, a value-based tool that helps educators identify areas in their courses where improvements can increase both social impact and student learning outcomes. 
To make this process systematic, we created a structured (Manual for Designing Digital Community Engagement Courses) to further assist educators in applying this approach.
By piloting selected courses, we were able to test, refine, and validate the Value Maps, the Manual, and the DICE Accelerator itself.
Last but not least, the project sought to generate sustainable impact by producing two key deliverables— the Best Practices Report and the DICE Handbook—which compile lessons learned, successful practices, and policy recommendations for integrating DICE courses into higher education systems
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectDescriptionImplementation:
WP1: TUKE created the Project Management Handbook, promo video, and coordinated Interim and Final reports. IUL, as dissemination leader, prepared the dissemination and sustainability strategy, website, social media, and promotional materials. ACEEU, as QA leader, produced e-newsletters, the QA strategy with an Impact Vision Plan, and all QA evaluations. TUKE and ACEEU conducted progress evaluations.
WP2: TUKE led WP2, including the Literature Review for Value Maps and a student survey. ACEEU developed the content management system for Value Maps. TUKE focused on Value Maps for Student Learning, while IUL led Value Maps for Social Impact. ACEEU created and validated the Value Maps prototype.
WP3: HELIX developed the Manual for Designing Digital Community Engagement Courses. ACEEU led the Accelerator creation – technical specifications, planning, platform development, and testing.
WP4: UAH led all WP4 activities—preparation, educator workshop, and piloting. Based on results, the Accelerator was refined and validated. UAH also prepared the Best Practices Report with support from all partners.
WP5: HELIX coordinated the DICE Handbook creation and Launch Event, with contributions from all partners and support from ACEEU.
a9fb935f-fd48-4deb-81c2-a7bf5921a989.projectDescriptionResults:
The DICE project delivered the following key outputs:
WP1: Project Management Handbook, Dissemination Strategy, project website, promotional materials, and Sustainability Strategy.
WP2: Literature Review for Value Maps (report covering 5 project countries and Europe), DICE Country Reports (state-of-the-art of DICE in partner countries), Student Survey Report (student perspectives on DICE), and two Value Maps (Social Impact and Student Learning).
WP3: Manual for Designing Digital Community Engagement Courses – a guide for educators to create innovative courses using the Accelerator and Digital Accelerator – an online platform providing a self-guided structure for developing courses with digital community engagement elements
WP4: Digital Accelerator Workshop for educators to prepare them for piloting and a Best Practice Report with best practices and lessons learned collected during piloting and throughout project implementation.
WP5: DICE Handbook – strategies and policy recommendations for integrating DICE into university structures, and the DICE Launch Event – a virtual event for stakeholders to share best practices and promote DICE results, especially the Accelerator.

f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectTitle: ErgoDesign – Improving digital skills for Ergonomics and Bioengineering Innovations for inclusive Health Care
f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectTags: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses|Digital skills and competences

f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectDescriptionBackground:
During the Covid pandemic the entire world experienced how important health care is and what happens when other values replace the priority of safeguarding human lives. It became clear that Health Care must be inclusive, thus allowing everyone to be able to access medical cures, both in times of emergency or in the phase of prevention. However, the reality is that few countries provide adequate quality services for people with disabilities.
The ErgoDesign project aimed at creating a new interdisciplinary Curriculum to cover different topics (from ergonomics to bioengineering), taking into consideration the requirements of people with special needs, to create a more inclusive care system. The project succeeded to increase the inclusion and diversity, improving the competencies of designer and producer 3D implants for medical purposes. The project contributed to create a more inclusive environment that is responsive to the needs of the wider community, including people with special needs. The analysis on the actual needs of the MedTech and BioTech sector for new employees demonstrated that the most important hard skills refer to design experience and experience with relevant software.
f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectDescriptionObjectives: The project partners have brought together their competencies into a new e-learning course, based on a student-centred approach and mixing both theory and practical exercises, to train a new generation of medical and technical staff able to boost the innovation in the medical plants sector. Also, partners felt the need of answering to an unsolved social issue related to the requirements of people with special needs (physical or mental diseases) that are prevented from accessing cures due to their disabilities. This aspect was included as transversal priority in the development of the project training contents and was addressed in a specific module included in the full curriculum. The project successfully transferred such knowledge and skills to both students and to HE lecturers/academics. The general objective of the project was to support the introduction of ergonomic and bioengineering innovations in implantology and prosthetics by adopting new digital applications and training in their use. The ErgoDesign e-learning course aimed also at filling this knowledge gap delivering a student- centred course mixing both theory and practical exercises for practicing digital skills and boosting students’ employability.
f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The specific objectives were: to increase the students’ knowledge in the field of ergonomics and bio-engineering and their digital skills for designing and producing related 3D printed medical products (dental and orthopedic implants, prostheses and exoskeletons, etc.) (SO1); to increase the knowledge necessary for the design of healthcare implants for people with special needs (physical and mental) (SO2); to extend the trainers’ knowledge of software/digital tools and their possibilities of use and adaptation for training (SO3); to increase the employability of the students in the medical implants sector (SO4); to create a community of practice around the topics of ergonomics and bioengineering (SO5).
The project has created a community of practice around the topics of ergonomics and bioengineering to communicate on an online collaborative platform, which is fed with training contents, as well as information and knowledge from stakeholders. The platform was designed to facilitate interaction and the sharing of resources. In order to achieve the project objectives, the partners followed a development path: they created a selection of software and digital tools aimed at enhancing the knowledge and digital skills of students and EU lecturers; they defined the main elements on which to build the training courses; they created supporting materials (Handbook and e-learning course), translated into seven different languages, to facilitate the replication of ErgoDesign-like courses by other stakeholders. Additionally, 7 webinars were organized to promote the dissemination of the knowledge and methodologies developed.
f7aa32cb-aa05-4986-b114-81d5d96c8cf1.projectDescriptionResults:
The partners developed 5 project results: 
PR1 – A Specialized software for design in the Health Care sector dynamic toolkit aimed at presenting several software/digital tools for booting digital competencies of HE lecturers/Academics and students.
PR2 – Course Design Principles and ErgoDesign Curriculum aimed at defining the
principles on which to build the multidisciplinary curriculum (topics, learning outcomes, duration, etc.).
PR3 – A Collaborative Platform, aimed at creating a space for discussion and training for stakeholders, hosting the virtual community of practices. https://ergodesigner.tu-varna.bg/
PR4 - ErgoDesign Training Materials, aimed at filling the knowledge and skill gaps of the students, by providing them with theoretical formation and practical exercises.
The lessons were divided into 11 modules and teaching materials were distributed for each module to fill the gaps in students' knowledge and skills, providing them with theoretical training and practical exercises.
The teaching materials are: 
- Manufacture of Metals for Biomedical Applications
- 3D printing of the metals, ceramics and polymers
- Anatomy of the implantology, geometry, sizes and general and special examples
- Material selection for implant
- Human implant compatibility test methods and surgery in implantology
- Databases, programming, AI
- Telemedicine system, medical informatics
- 3D scanning, process and device
- Medical Imaging (CT/MRI/USG)
- Application of the 3D images for designing as a function of the processing technology (digital tools for designing)
- Medical equipment, hospital equipment for people with special needs
For each module there are assessments. The entire module was developed on moodle open source and is therefore easily replicable also on third-party platforms. 
PR5 - Handbook and e-learning course,aimed at creating resources to ease the replication of the ErgoDesign course by other organizations. The Handbook translated into seven different languages, including Greek, Slovak, Polish,  Hungarian, Italian, Bulgarian and English. 
With reference to PR1 and PR4, the digital pedagogical skills of HE teachers in the areas of 3D design and production of sanitary facilities have increased and have increased HE students’ digital skills.

34de0881-97b0-4b37-be91-bad584543b07.projectDescriptionBackground: The goal of the project was to focus on the transfer of technology and the protection of intellectual property, on supporting the creation  of a business environment based on the results of science and research with individual tools, and on supporting the creation of spin-off companies as business entities established for the commercialization of intellectual property created at the university. The implementation of this project strengthened the institutional cooperation between the University of Hradec Králové and the University of Granada and the Technical University of Košice at the level of education and cooperation in the field of intellectual property. We applied for this project because, according to the needs analysis (made before the project started), there was a lack of educational materials in the field of transfer technology, a lack of methodologies to effectively support the creation of a spin-off and there was no summer school focused on this topic. It was also important to implement a new subject that will cover this field.
34de0881-97b0-4b37-be91-bad584543b07.projectDescriptionObjectives: UHK managed to find strong partners for solving the relevant topic. By implementing the project, the beneficiary wanted to connect experience and knowledge in the field of technology transfer and transform it into reproducible outputs. The consortium wanted to achieve the creation of an effective course focused on technology transfer, to create a methodology supporting the creation of spin-off companies in an academic environment and to establish a tradition of organizing a summer school focused on technology transfer.
34de0881-97b0-4b37-be91-bad584543b07.projectDescriptionImplementation: Activities within the project were implemented exactly according to the approved project proposal. For the first time, an innovative approach to transfer technology was applied at the top management level, where rectors and vice-rectors were directly involved. For the first time, technology transfer was addressed at the top management level of three international universities. The institutional cooperation project envisaged relevant activities between all three partners, which provided a valuable opportunity to share their expertise in knowledge transfer and technology transfer and spin-off establishment methodology and support the development of innovative joint educational modules of intellectual property and knowledge transfer education and technology. And thanks to the involvement of the top management of all three partners, high quality results were achieved at the rectorate level with a real impact on the university environment. On behalf of UHK, the Rector Prof. Kamil Kuča and the Vice-Rectors Dr. Leona Stašová, Prof. Ondřej Krejcar and Prof. Petra Marešová, on behalf of TUKE the Vice-Rector Prof. Radovan Hudák and on behalf of UGR the Vice-Rector Prof. Enrique Herrera Viedma.
34de0881-97b0-4b37-be91-bad584543b07.projectDescriptionResults:
The project aimed to achieve 6 intellectual outputs. Despite the unfavorable situation at the beginning of the project solution caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, the consortium managed to work effectively on the project and all outputs were achieved.
The goals of the project were achieved by developing the following intellectual outputs (IO):
O1 The curriculum of the course Technology transfer for students, academics, researchers and university staff
O2 Syllabi for the course Transfer technology for students, academics and researchers 
O3 Methodology for successful spin off setting in academic area 
O4 Methodology_Summer school _Transfer technology_ Training programmes 
O5 Technology transfer pilot course 
O6 Transfer technology – methodology for top management of university
The instructions are accompanied by several instructional materials and infographics that can help as a brief introduction and demonstration of the basic principles of teaching transfer technology and creating spin-offs. All outputs produced by the project will remain freely available on the project website and a platform for the dissemination of the results of the Erasmus+ program.

results.resultTitle: IO1 – The curriculum of the course Technology transfer for students, academics, researchers  and university staff
results.resultDescription: During the implementation of the project, an innovative curriculum for the subject and course Transfer Technology was created for students, academics, researchers and university employees. The curriculum was expanded and supplemented by the observation of the technology transfer sector with the comments of experts from both partner organizations. The curriculum is focused on technology transfer, intellectual property protection and support of spin-off companies within the framework of setting the curriculum for the interactive course. First, a thorough search of existing training courses in the field of technology transfer and intellectual property issues was carried out, and a methodological and didactic approach was also implemented. The teaching is mainly focused on the business and financial plan, project management and risk management, the output of creative activity and its financing and the protection of the output according to copyright.
results.resultCategory: Others

results.resultTitle: IO2 – Syllabi for the course Transfer technology for students, academics and researchers
results.resultDescription:
IO2 was created in relation to the innovative curriculum of the course " Technology transfer for students, academics, researchers and university staff". The course combines lecture, audio-visual methods and discussion and other forms. With regard to the target group of the course, i.e. scientists, young researchers or other bearers of innovative ideas, there is space for discussion on the above topics in relation to the issue and topic of the participant himself. Lectures will be led by experts in the field, all supported by materials in an e-learning environment, and discussions will be organized both in groups and individually according to the needs of individual participants.
Due to the large number of attachments to this output, they have not been uploaded directly here, but are available on the project website: https://www.uhk.cz/en/university-of-hradec-kralove/research/programs-projects-and-competitions/eu-international-projects/technology-transfer-together/intellectual-outputs
results.resultCategory: Others

results.resultTitle: IO3 – Methodology for successful spin off setting in academic area
results.resultDescription: The methodology guides the reader through all the essential knowledge, skills and digital competencies that a potential spin-off founder is looking for. It looks at the overall perception and understanding of spin-offs, describes the key ones considerations related to the creation and management of spin-offs, provides an analysis of data and introduces a methodology for the creation of spin-offs. Critical points in the methodology were identified in the entire process of setting up the spin-off company and the process was described in a holistic approach. The methodology also deals with some key motivational mechanisms for promoting entrepreneurial thinking in the academic environment and contributes to spin-offs. Because the commercialization of research results or intellectual property created at universities facilitates the application of new technologies in the world and contributes to economic growth, academic spin-offs are a key element of the innovation ecosystem.
results.resultCategory: Others

results.resultTitle: IO4 – Methodology Summer School – Technology Transfer Training Program
results.resultDescription: The document deals with the overall perception and understanding of summer school organizations at universities. It describes the key considerations associated with the organization of summer schools, the motivation for its organization, content, etc. and presents the background of the summer school and offers answers to the most important questions that the university should ask itself before starting it. The question of the budget and the total amount for the organization of the summer school is also important, according to which the course fee should be determined at the beginning. The methodology introduces the reader to how to attract potential students. 219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectTitle: Digital Area for Networking Teachers and Educators
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectTags: Open and distance learning|ICT - new technologies - digital competences|New innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectDescriptionBackground:
Digital competence DC - (as described by European Commision (EC) in European Digital Competence Framework – DigComp) is “a multi-dimensional construct that includes knowledge, skills and attitudes in a
range of areas, including creative use of digital technologies, safe and responsible use and data literacy.
Within DigComp, digital competence is defined as the confident, critical and responsible use of digital technologies for learning, work, and participation in society. This understanding of DC has been further elaborated featuring 21 competencies described under five ‘main competence areas’: information and data literacy, communication and collaboration, digital content creation, safety and problem-solving.

We all should learn from the COVID-19 crisis as it pushed all of us to use the ICT technologies in a massive way and we should be prepared for the future. The EC also puts a great
emphasis to the infrastructure, connectivity and digital equipment, effective digital capacity planning and development, education of digitally competent and confident teachers and
development of high-quality teaching content, user-friendly tools and secure platforms.
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The main objective/idea of the DANTE project was the support of HEI education through a project supporting digital competencies among teachers, academic staff and university students and
establishing a cooperative network among educational institutions. Outputs will help HEIs to increase the quality of teaching and attractiveness of study and improve skills and capacities of educators.

The key area was to support the skills and competencies mentioned above and this is where the partners of the project (universities from 5 different countries) aimed their activities.

Although the universities are ready to provide high-quality education to their students, thanks to the situation that were facing during the coronavirus pandemy, the education
strategies, approaches and methodologies had to be adjusted to that situation. It was necessary to provide university teachers with the necessary knowledge, skills, equipment and
sources needed to smooth switch from the face-to-face teaching to digital (online) education.
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectDescriptionImplementation:
During the course of the DANTE project, we assumed that in order to make a meaningful impact on HEIs and digital education, different stakeholders should be approached and engaged in the project activities. Therefore, we placed special emphasis on the continuous involvement of HEI teachers and HEI students mostly from partnering HEIs but also externals. As a first step, we designed and performed a survey of all major stakeholders in higher education. Based on these, we started to develop guidelines how to deal with digital education and communication within higher education. 

Within DANTE, we have created 4 different types of guidelines accompanied by instructional videos and infographics. 

During the development, we continuously piloted our outputs, both among students and educators. We also created set of courses with specific contents - that can be customized through Moodle platform - as intended by the teacher. All guidelines, videos and infographics are available on the project webpage. In addition, we have developed, using LMS Moodle, a platform for piloting the courses and showing the project outputs to both external and internal educators.
219ada45-ebe8-48ab-a0b4-9211a8f86e83.projectDescriptionResults:
The objectives of the project were achieved through the development of the following intellectual outputs (IO):

IO1: DANTE market research and survey report
IO2: DANTE guidelines HOW TO develop a digital course
IO3: DANTE guidelines HOW TO set up the IT infrastructure for digital education
IO4: DANTE guidelines HOW TO communicate with students and motivate them in digital education
IO5: DANTE digital courses in the fields of Business and Economics

The guidelines are accompanied by several instructional videos and infographics that can help as a brief introduction and demonstration of the core principles of digital education and communication.

All outputs created by the project will remain available on the project website which will be maintained for a minimum of 3 years after the project ends. From the website, all project outputs are freely available

The project and its outputs has been widely presented and disseminated to the defined target groups during offline and online events on local, national and international level.

results.resultTitle: How to communicate with students in digital education
results.resultDescription:
Practical guide for teachers on communication with students.
One of the aims of the DANTE project was to develop new solutions that could support the communication in the digital environment while teaching. To develop the proposed solutions we have applied various methodologies, to revise the opinions, ideas and suggestions of the students and teachers from the partner Universities, to identify the potential areas of concern in digital communication (in particular those that emerged during pandemic) and the possible routes to its improvement. We have also revised the existing academic literature (and the empirical evidence within) to track the communication styles that have been confirmed to be efficient in the digital environment.

Based on this work, we developed the final set of guidelines to address the proper communication tools and communication styles, to enhance the learning outcomes in digital education.

e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectTitle: Art & Creative Craft Enterprises for Successful Streaming of 3D Printing
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectTags: ICT - new technologies - digital competences|New innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses|Enterprise, industry and SMEs (incl. entrepreneurship)
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectLevel3Label: Strategic Partnerships for vocational education and training
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectDescriptionBackground:
Additive manufacturing (or 3D printing) is a promising and strategic technology on the European market, which is increasingly adopted by small craft companies with significant creative capacity. This technology allows them to strengthen their competitiveness and can easily be adopted by more traditional craft companies.

Nevertheless, to be able to maximize the benefits and develop an innovative customizable offer, adapted to market needs, it requires being equipped with immediately usable technical and creative skills. More specifically, it requires investing in physical capital (machines) and training human capital through training dedicated to craft companies and adapted to the market.

Based on this observation, we decided to carry out a project with the objective to contribute to the definition of a training framework on 3D printing, allowing companies and future entrepreneurs to develop their technical skills, their creative, innovative, and entrepreneurial capacities, to apply innovative ideas in the craft sector.
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectDescriptionObjectives:
Our project aimed to set out frameworks providing the basis to train and upskills craft companies regarding 3D printing and advanced industrial robotics. More specifically, the expected results of the project were to: 
1.To innovate and inter-connect creative and traditional craft companies by studying the training offer in Europe and by identifying the gaps between the skills needs of professionals and the existing training offer in 3D printing and robotics.
2. Use the skills needs to develop and tailored VET curricula according to EUI standards to foster the mobility and employability in the craft sector in Europe
3. Improve the competitiveness and efficiency of the traditional craft companies using 3D printing technologies.
4. Improve the entrepreneurship in the craft sector and additive manufacturing sector through better understanding of the 3D printing value chain
5. Evaluate the impact of tailored training about 3D printing on entrepreneurs and craftsmen.
6. Sustain the project results, in the course of time, through the development recommendations for certification.
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectDescriptionImplementation:
To reach the expected results, we developed and carried out the following activities:
1. A comparative study of 3D printing training programs in Europe and identification of training needs for the craft companies that are wishing to adopt this technology.
2. Design of a joint VET curriculum on 3D printing techniques for craft companies.
3. Development and integration of learning modules on 3D printing and its application for craft companies on a MOOC (Massive Open On-line Course) platform. 
4. Test and validation of innovative tools with an audience of craft companies and relative stakeholders.
e06287a7-0ddb-4397-a96a-da0d52ca59ff.projectDescriptionResults:
1. Study report on 3D printing training programs in Europe and identification of the training needs of craft companies wishing to adopt this technology. Study report to understand how vocational training actors can innovate and inter-connect creative craftsmen and traditional craftsmen through 3D printing.
2. Design of a joint VET curriculum on 3D printing. Report on the full curriculum and on the validation process, with an overview of the national education framework in France, Spain, Portugal, Slovakia, and Slovenia. User guide for trainers and report on the open education resources strategy. 
3. Online learning platform including 6 learning modules enriched with examples to better understand 3D printing technology. A full learning programme accounting for 250 hours of study, entitling to 15 ECVET points (EQF level 5)
4. Report on the methodology and piloting phase put in place by the partners to test and validate the learning platform and its modules. Study report on the piloting activities, on the feedback collected and the changes integrated to the platform.

dc078dac-a354-4eef-a3d5-4ddf83dacf5a.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
dc078dac-a354-4eef-a3d5-4ddf83dacf5a.projectDescriptionBackground:
The rapid ageing of the population does not only concern Europe, but it´s spreading worldwide. In 2020 third of the working population was over 55 years old. This means that we are currently facing a situation we have never dealt with before – more than four generations can find themselves working together at the same company, thus creating a multigenerational workforce. As each generation has its own work pace, procedures, and uses different communication strategies, it is not uncommon that conflicts occur, older employees face segregation or even leave and companies have high turnover. At the same time, every sector is changing due to digitalisation and the influence of Industry 4.0. Hence the growing body of workforce above 55 must adapt rapidly to the constantly growing demands of the labour market to be „fluent“ in digital technologies. A one-size-fits-all approach will fail companies in their attempt to resolve this situation.
That is why INSPIRER project aims to bring necessary tools and activities to promote the creation of a healthy multigenerational workplace culture in companies and foster the development of digital skills.
dc078dac-a354-4eef-a3d5-4ddf83dacf5a.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The primary objective of the project is to foster the adoption of shared values, equality, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace using innovative approaches and tools. By the INSPIRER project implementation the project partners wanted to reach the following objectives:
·      mitigate ageism and segregation in the workplace, inevitably leading to high turnover of the employees
·      create more positive and inclusive working environment for people of all age
·      train company and HR managers on how to create and maintain a multigenerational workforce
·      upskill senior employees with up-to-date digital skills
·      upskill younger employees with interpersonal skills
·      create a more flexible working mindset of older generations
·      involve all stakeholders and provide practical tools for the assessment of multigenerational culture in the workplace
dc078dac-a354-4eef-a3d5-4ddf83dacf5a.projectDescriptionImplementation: The project executed targeted activities to reach a large number of stakeholders inside and outside of companies, such as policymakers, chambers, associations, SMEs and larger companies, company and HR managers, and employees, thanks to an extensive network of partners. By creating an online course, the company and HR managers gained knowledge on how to foster and build and sustain an effective multigenerational workplace. A 360o assessment tool for multigenerational workplace culture was developed and offered to companies. This tool allows them to evaluate the elements of multigenerational workplace culture from the perspective of managers and employees above and under 55 years. Via the creation of a mentorship model and mentoring guide, awareness was raised on the concept of cross-generational / reverse-age mentorships. What´s more, guide offers a step-by-step instruction on how to create a reverse-age mentoring.  A mentorship platform was developed to offer a safe space for employees of different ages to collaborate and exchange knowledge on various topics. Partners organised webinars and multiplier events where the project results were disseminated, and participants were recruited to join the piloting.
dc078dac-a354-4eef-a3d5-4ddf83dacf5a.projectDescriptionResults:
Within the project 3 main outputs were created: 
•	Training course on multigenerational workplace culture for the company and HR managers. Course provides useful information and training on elements and policies which need to be implemented in companies to profit from the full potential of supporting a multigenerational culture in their respective environment.  
•	360o assessment tool for multigenerational workplace culture. The tool provides a holistic approach to assessing the culture of a company. It allows company managers and employees (both above and under 55 years) to measure the elements that constitute a multigenerational workplace and it provides suggestions and tips on how to enhance the multigenerational culture in the workplace. 
•	Cross-generational / reverse-age mentorships in digital technologies. This output raises awareness of the concept of reverse mentoring. It also provides a safe space where younger and older employees can pair and provide mentoring to each other by sharing their respective expertise (e.g., on new technologies). 
Project consortium managed to raise awareness of the importance of creating a multigenerational workplace culture by engaging and bringing together older and younger employees.

2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectTitle: Construction Safety with Education and Training using Immersive Reality
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectTags: New innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses|Health and wellbeing|ICT - new technologies - digital competences
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectDescriptionBackground:
Construction industry represents one of the most dangerous industries in terms of OHS. The construction site is a dynamic and complex environment, which makes it difficult to manage and monitor. Ensuring a safe working environment, i.e. the construction site and the construction process, prevents occupational accidents and even deaths. It is a socially topical topic that persists despite several initiatives. It is also an economic problem that costs about 4% of world GDP. In the XXI. century, it is unacceptable for a worker to be fatally injured during the performance of his work. 
Safety challenges are particularly significant for new and often low-skilled workers due to a lack of training. Injuries and accidents occur because workers are not properly trained in occupational safety. Every construction site is different, so technicians, workers and engineers need to be trained on the unique and potential risks that can arise from each new environment. In order to prevent the emergence of safety risks on construction sites, it is not possible to rely only on traditional, current measures for their prevention.
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The CSETIR project (Construction Safety with Education and Training using Immersive Reality) is based on the synergy between higher education institutions and representatives of construction practice. The goal was to introduce the use of intelligent technologies in the proper training process for the elimination of safety risks in the construction industry. The effort is the implementation of digital tools that enable the creation of a virtual environment that simulates construction scenarios and enables teachers, instructors, technicians and engineers to identify and prevent safety risks.
The aim of the project was also to improve the exchange of knowledge between representatives of the three sectors with the aim of innovating approaches to accident prevention through effective cooperation between researchers in the field of virtual reality and construction companies. The CSETIR partnership has developed innovative and interactive VR/AR (virtual and augmented reality) solutions for the prevention of construction site accidents. CSETIR has created a useful tool for teachers, technicians and engineers that can be used in any construction project. The created digital tool with study materials is accessible online on the web site.
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The CSETIR project was focused on the creation of a digital education tool for the elimination of safety risks on the construction site. In order to create the tool, it was necessary to analyze the issue of construction safety, the issue of a suitable ICT tool for VR/AR with immersive elements, the possibilities of processing the construction process using building information modeling. 18 safety risk scenarios on the construction site were processed, divided into 6 basic groups, e.g. 4 scenarios related to falling from a height, etc.; and their subsequent description for visualization in a VR environment. The correct use of the created digital tool is supported by the creation of manuals for its use for teachers and students. Of course, the project outputs are available on the project website.
Part of the project solution were activities connected with project management, distribution and management of specific partial project tasks, coordination of their fulfillment, creation of communication channels between the solvers, dissemination activities and project monitoring. The project managers also participated in 7 transnational project meetings (4 face-to-face + 3 online).
2e865c17-c7f8-4812-9e16-a6d8a937ec1f.projectDescriptionResults:
The project outputs were focused on 5 intellectual outputs - IO1- Necessary analyses, IO2 BIM models, IO3 interactive VR/AR solutions, IO4 Teaching manual and IO5 Online platform. The project was not focused on multiplication events or teaching and training activities.
Intellectual output 1 (IO1) was processed in the form of a report in five language versions (in English, Slovak, Portuguese, Croatian and Greek). It contains overviews, analyzes and knowledge of all project solvers related to the field of health and safety in the construction industry, the use of augmented, mixed and virtual reality for possible project solutions, building information modeling (BIM). In IO2, BIM models of construction sites and a library of construction site equipment objects focused mainly on safety are processed. IO3 contains a proposed digital tool for the elimination of safety risks at the construction site in a collaborative virtual environment enabling interaction in the virtual space between multiple participants; and a description of the visualization of security risk scenarios. IO4 provides training manuals for using the developed digital tool. IO5 provides an online platform for accessing project outputs and results in several formats.

9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectTitle: Education of Future ICT Experts Based on Smart Society Needs
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectTags: New innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses|ICT - new technologies - digital competences|Entrepreneurial learning - entrepreneurship education
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectDescriptionBackground:
ICT curricula at HEIs traditionally have STEM content. There are different options in which direction the “new-born” ICT experts can continue in their careers after graduation. They often become new entrepreneurs. Our primary motivation for applying for our project was tackling skills gaps and creating a new innovative course focused on ICT-based entrepreneurship. Another motivation was implementing an intensive interdisciplinary and intercultural study environment and promoting internationalisation. We wanted to contribute to open education and innovative practices in a digital era by creating a vital extension to the education of future ICT experts.
An online survey was conducted in February and March 2019. Two questionnaires were designed - ICT companies and students. Based on the responses of IT companies, it can be noted that when they are recruiting new employees, they attach great importance, in addition to IT skills, to the transfer of skills and business skills. Other factors included digital skills, networking, and language skills. For students, it is crucial to have the possibility to learn Project Management and Planning, Delegation and Time Management, Team Management, Communication and Negotiation skills.
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The main objective of our project was to enforce ICT student teams to deal with economic, societal, and environmental challenges by introducing entrepreneurial learning that follows and respects the UN's and EU's current strategic documents. We wanted to prepare and develop training courses covering ICT, new technologies and digital competencies that are important when creating new business plans for ICT students' start-ups. 
We wanted to give the project participants chance to collaborate with colleagues from different European universities on an entrepreneurial case related to recognising the needs of society and providing a smart solution by using ICT. We wanted to promote internationalisation. We wanted to achieve and push our project participants to  "go out of the box" of their traditional education (STEM) by giving them some basic knowledge and experience of project-based learning, student teamwork, and blended mobility through developing specific entrepreneurial cases for Smart Society domain.
We wanted to develop educational materials that support additional education in the field of business. These educational materials were prepared for the educational process at HEIs at the ICT-oriented schools and faculties.
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectDescriptionImplementation:
We implemented different activities related to project management, development of educational materials, multiplying of project impact, learning, teaching and training of ICT-oriented entrepreneurship.
Our activities related to project management were covered by 8 transnational project meetings (2 online). Our activities related to the development of educational materials were covered by intellectual outputs: IO1 Entrepreneurial cases: "entrepreneurship in ICT" and "entrepreneurship with ICT", IO2 SmartSoc proceedings, IO3 SmartSoc E-learning Platform. Our activities related to multiplying the project impact were covered by 3 multiplier events. Our project activities related to learning, teaching and training activities were organised as blended mobilities. We organised our blended mobilities three times – in 2020, 2021 and 2022. The blended mobility itself was adapted to the duration of one semester. Two phases of blended mobility were planned for the 13-week - virtual and physical. The virtual part lasted 10 weeks and the physical part 2 weeks. There was one spare week to complete the tasks from the virtual part, if a student team needed it, between them. The blended mobility completion was planned for late May by the workshop.
9d473530-c081-42b4-b5c4-007695e70eb3.projectDescriptionResults:
We developed three independent adaptations of an interdisciplinary and intercultural course focused on the entrepreneurship education of ICT students. Each version is an output of one year of blended mobility that was introduced as a new educational method. Proposals of entrepreneurial cases prepared for student teams and a brief overview of business plans and business model canvases of virtual start-up-s are recorded in the Intellectual output 1 (pdf document published on the project web). Lectures of experts from our workshops (Intellectual Output 2) are recorded, and related presentations are uploaded to the project e-learning portal (Intellectual Output 3). Lectures are our Intellectual output 2. All these outputs are our contribution to open education and innovative practices in a digital era. They are free for everyone interested.
Our project results enable us to bring novelties regarding topics under consideration, i.e., ICT expertise related to smart society needs, with a particular emphasis on entrepreneurship and skills related to evaluation of business perspectives and societal implications of the proposed solution, respecting relevant smart specialisation strategies defined in the EU at different geographical levels.

81c93bd0-41f2-4a22-91e6-52eb3760d927.projectDescriptionBackground: Industry 4 is transforming industries at an unprecedented rate. New technologies, new principles and methods of its operation are entering production. This has an impact on changing job positions and their content. As a result, new workforce knowledge requirements are emerging from new technologies such as: Internet of Things, Big Data, Advanced Robotics, Additive Manufacturing, Digital Twin, Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence. New job positions are being created, such as "worker 4", "mechatronics 4", "engineering 4", but the profile of education is also changing to "Education 4". In the dynamics of this development, man has become the weakest point to achieve efficient smart production. This development shows that existing knowledge is no longer sufficient. The problem is that many schools do not systematically prepare their graduates with knowledge of Industry 4 and advanced technologies to increase their competitiveness in the labour market. But for the companies, the Industry 4 theme is highly actual and a workforce with industry 4 knowledge is in high demand. Another reason for solving the project was to find out the unflattering state of readiness of many schools to provide new knowledge. Another problem has been that many teachers and VET trainers do not have sufficient depth of knowledge from the field of Industry 4, but especially from the principles and methods of new production and the use of new technologies. The reason for solving the project was also that the emerging trends clearly provoke the innovation of vocational education in the field of vocational training of vocational school graduates. For these reasons, the project focused primarily on vocational and secondary school teachers teaching mainly subjects profiling graduates for production practice as the main target group. The changes that current production is undergoing also point to the need to prepare a larger number of high school graduates with knowledge and skills to work with new technologies for the digital production era. Applying for a project focusing on the preparation of study materials from Industry 4 technologies for vocational teachers was therefore a clear choice, because it is VET teachers who must be in the first place to be knowledgeable but also skilfully prepared to educate their students for the new generation of production- smart production. It follows that tomorrow's workers must have the technical skills and competences which must be complemented by dexterity in thinking and problem-solving skills. The current workforce must immediately start training and retraining to be competent for Industry 4.0 era.
81c93bd0-41f2-4a22-91e6-52eb3760d927.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The trends are clear: human labour will continue to play a key role in Industry 4.0. However, the type of work will change fundamentally, and so will the skills needed to do it. The project wanted to provide a comprehensive view of the concept of the 4th Industrial Revolution, show the changes that new technologies bring and how they change the content of knowledge for emerging jobs, but mainly give teachers of secondary and higher education study lessons which deal with these new technologies. The project wanted to show some good examples that many manufacturing companies had already used or had already implemented new technologies to increase their efficiency and competitiveness.
The education system is not always able to keep up with the evolving labour market. Therefore, it fails to provide companies with a highly skilled and prepared workforce in a timely manner. Therefore, the project wanted to provide study material in advance in the form of lessons to teachers of vocational schools but also to educational institutions on the emerging trend of development of production systems.
The main goals of the project were to implement new knowledge from Industry 4 into vocational education as soon as possible and thus to prepare and put into practice professional graduates, able to work with new technologies and accelerate transformation and digitization in production with production with high adaptability and connectivity. It is logical that if the project wanted to meet these goals it had to achieve that just teachers and coaches of vocational training will be provided, to an appropriate extent and in sufficient depth, with study materials from the new ones approaches and technologies of Industry 4 in such a form that they can be used immediately or transformed into their curriculum.
The project also sought to bring worker 4 into production as soon as possible and to introduce new-innovative technologies that fundamentally change the structures, connectivity and operation of production, enabling the production of new, highly innovative products with an Internet connection and intelligent functions meeting individual customer requirements.
One of the priority goals of the project from the beginning of the solution was to achieve the widest possible awareness of Industry 4 in both professional and common society as well as among students through direct contacts as well as through leaflets, brochures, conferences and workshops. Awareness-raising and education for Industry 4 project was considered as important steps to support Industry 4.0.
81c93bd0-41f2-4a22-91e6-52eb3760d927.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The main activity of the project was focused mainly on the development of intellectual outputs focused on showing good examples of educational practice for Industry 4, to give a systemic view of the concept of Industry 4 and to develop lessons about the technological pillars of Industry 4.
Leaflet No. 1, leaflet No. 2 and a brochure, which contain the content of the most important project´s functions have been developed to raise awareness of Industry 4 as much as possible and also to inform about the objectives and results of the project. Furthermore, a website was created with the most important information and events that took place during the project. The leaflets, brochure and website were created in all languages of the partnership and in English. The presentation of the project was at various events such as OPTIROB international conference, the School for the 21st Century conference, at student competitions, at meetings with education staff, professional and public associations and local governments. The activities of the dissemination workshops were aimed at presenting, testing and receiving feedback from the lessons. For Secondary School in Bardejov, the priority activities were the provision of project materials as well as their own experience with the implementation of already achieved project results and feedback from cooperating companies in which their students practice. The partners from the universities directed their activities to secondary schools, with which they have a long-term cooperation and where they promote their studies. Their activities in disseminating and using the results of the project on university grounds were a matter of course. As a result of these activities, all partners have innovated curricula in their fields and approaches to building laboratories for acquiring practical skills. 
Within the project, two professional training courses for employees of partner organizations were also implemented. The first vocational training was focused on the system and methodology of using and creating TI4 e-learning courses in the Coursevo platform. The basis of the second vocational training was the technology of the Internet of Things and collaborative robotics, in which the partners showed the greatest interest due to the acquisition of detailed knowledge and their use both in the educational process and for expanding research activities.
81c93bd0-41f2-4a22-91e6-52eb3760d927.projectDescriptionResults:
The results of the project are based on the current needs of industry and schools for the main target groups, which are secondary vocational school teachers and their students. The specific intellectual outputs of the project are:
The intellectual output of the project O1-Examples of good practice is focused on the content: 1. Examples of best practices of Industry 4 in education, 2. Examples of best practices of implementation of Industry 4 technologies in practice. Intellectual output O2-Industry 4 provides information on developments during the Industrial Revolutions up to the 4th Industrial Revolution, explains the concept and philosophy of Industry 4, defines cyber-physical systems, describes the principles of intelligent production, major technologies and also lists the benefits and risks of new production and requirements to the new content of knowledge and skills. The intellectual output O3-Technology Industry 4 has 8 modules and each module has 2-3 lessons written in 4 languages (English, Greek, Polish, Slovak).
Module no.1: Internet of Things. Lessons: 1.1 Internet of Things, industrial Internet of Things, 1.2 Automatic data collection from production.
Module no. 2: Advanced robotics. Lessons: 2.1 Industrial Robotics, 2.2 Collaborative Robots and 2.3 Bin Picking Robotic Systems.
Module no. 3: Big data analysis. Lessons: 3.1 Introduction to big data analysis, 3.2 Visualization, process, tools and people. Privacy and 3.3 Big Data Industrial Applications and Use Cases.
Module no. 4: 3D printing, additive production: Lessons: 4.1 3D scanning - data acquisition method in reverse engineering, 4.2 Rapid prototyping. Reverse engineering, 4.3 Additive technology - 3D printing.
Module No. 5: Digital twin. Lessons: 5.1 Digital twins, 5.2 Tools for creating DT, 5.3 Methodical framework for creating digital twins.
Module No. 6: Virtual reality. Lessons: 6.1 Virtual reality, 6.2 Applications of virtual reality in production.
Module No.7: Artificial intelligence. Lessons: 7.1 Artificial intelligence in production, 7.2 Intelligent products, machines, robots, 7.3 Artificial intelligence methods used in production.
Thematic videos of knowledge and models to gain additional knowledge were also added. 
Intellectual output O4-ICT methodology. All education systems are implemented on a special multifunctional ICT platform for education and training COURSEVO. Intellectual Output O5-Glossary is a glossary of terms and expressions used in connection with the development of industry 4 and new technologies.
The publication outputs of the project were contributions:
1. in the journal Applied Computer Science registered in Scopus: CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGIES AS A KEY FACTOR IN THE PROCESS OF INDUSTRY 4.0 AND SMART MANUFACTURING DEVELOPMENT. The article emphasizes that the main technologies in the context of Industry 4.0 are cyber physical systems (CPS) and the Internet of Things (IoT). CPS considers IoT to be a key technology. In this way, products and means of production are interconnected and can "communicate", bringing new ways of production and real-time optimization.
2. at the international conference AUTOMATION 2022, in press: Change of current production to smart factory. The article emphasizes that production systems are extended by network connections enabling communication with other devices and output of information about them. This networking of all systems leads to intelligent factories in which production systems, components and people communicate through a network and production is almost autonomous.
In addition, two leaflets and a brochure with basic information on the project's objectives and outputs were created for dissemination, which were provided in personal and professional meetings and at various events, such as student competitions and open days at partner and collaborating schools, conferences.
Other concrete results of the project were workshops held in each partnership country, at which training lessons were presented and tested. The results of the questionnaire form of evaluation of the project lessons gave many suggestions for improving the content and graphics of the lesson.

results.resultTitle: Intelektuálny výstup O1: Príklady dobrej praxe- výstup v SK
results.resultDescription: Základnou schémou bolo:  Výstup uvádza  príklady realizácie a využívania jednotlivých technológií v praxi a vo vzdelávaní.Sú uvedené reálne  príklady implementácie a využívania ale hlavne opodstatnenosť nových technológií pre budúce smart výroby. Sú uvedené príklady, ktoré sú overené, sú vypracované renomovanými organizáciami a sú realizovateľné v cieľových skupinách.Takmer každý príklad zo vzdelávania ale aj z praxe poukazuje na vplyv na zmenu obsahu vzdelávania ale aj na zmenu prístupov a nových technológii a metód vzdelávania v  ére Industry 4 a smart výroby.   Komplexnosť tréningových procesov pre Industry 4 je dokumentovaná príkladmi  renomovaných organizácií  v oblasti vzdelávania pre automatizáciu ako je napr. FESTO. Výstup O1 preukazuje vecnú náplň začleňovania nových poznatkov z Industry 4 do vzdelávania, použiteľnosť nových didaktických pomôcok a tréningových stendov s prepojením na internet veci a tiež pre on-line tréning

results.resultTitle: Intelektuálny výstup O2-Industry 4- výstup v SK
results.resultDescription: Výstup Industry 4 poskytuje poznatky o všeobecnom vývoji do 4. priemyselnej revolúcie, vysvetľuje koncepciu a filozofiu I4, definuje kyberneticko-fyzikálne systémy, popisuje princípy inteligentnej výroby, hlavné črty používaných technológií a ich súvislosti, uvádza aj výhody a riziká novej výroby a požiadavky na nový obsah vedomostí a zručností pre nový rozsah práce. Výstup 02 Industry 4 predstavuje komplexný materiál o vývoji, trendoch a funkciách I 4. Ďalej je zdôraznené, že tento pokrok v súčasnosti vedie k vytvoreniu pracovného prostredia, v ktorom sa stretáva fyzický a virtuálny svet. Ľudia, stroje, objekty a systémy sú prepojené prostredníctvom IKT a internetu, dynamicky komunikujú v reálnom čase a organizujú a optimalizujú procesy.

results.resultTitle: Článok-CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGIES AS A KEY FACTOR IN THE PROCESS OF INDUSTRY 4.0 AND SMART MANUFACTURING DEVELOPMENT
results.resultDescription:
Jarosław ZUBRZYCKI, Antoni ŚWIĆ, Łukasz SOBASZEK, Juraj KOVAC, Ruzena KRALIKOVA, Robert JENCIk, Natalia SMIDOVA, Polyxeni ARAPI, Peter DULENCIN, Jozef HOMZA: CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGIES AS A KEY FACTOR IN THE PROCESS OF INDUSTRY 4.0 AND SMART MANUFACTURING DEVELOPMENT. In:  Applied Computer Science, vol. 17, no. 4, pp. 84–99, 2021
 
Článok zdôrazňuje, že hlavnými technológiami v kontexte Industry 4.0 sú kybernetické fyzické systémy (CPS) a internet vecí (IoT). CPS sa považujú za kľúčové technológie, ktoré majú vstavané softvérové systémy a disponujú internetovou adresou aby sa mohli pripojiť cez IoT. Týmto spôsobom sa produkty a výrobné prostriedky prepoja a môžu „komunikovať“, čo prináša  nové spôsoby výroby, vytváranie nových hodnôt a optimalizáciu v reálnom čase.
results.resultCategory: Dissemination material

results.resultTitle: Článok- Change of current production to smart factory
results.resultDescription:
Z. Pilat, M. Omieljanowicz, J. Zubrzycki, R. Jencik: Change of current production to smart factory. In. AUTOMATION 2022, v tlači.
 
 Článok zdôrazňuje, že výrobné systémy sa rozširujú  o sieťové pripojenia umožňujúce komunikáciu s inými zariadeniami a výstup informácií o nich. Toto sieťové prepojenie všetkých systémov vedie ku „kyberneticko-fyzikálnym výrobným systémom“, a teda k inteligentným továrňam, v ktorých výrobné systémy, komponenty a ľudia komunikujú prostredníctvom siete a výroba je takmer autonómna.
Článok zdôrazňuje, že Industry 4.0 je viac než len technológie. Ide o zásadné zmeny v spôsobe výroby, ide o robenie nových vecí, vytváranie nových produktov a poskytovanie informácií a riadenie celého životného cyklu výrobku.
results.resultCategory: Dissemination material

results.resultTitle: IO2 Digital training materials for start-uppers
results.resultDescription:
Digital training materials for start-uppers – set of Open Educational Resources (OERs) with m-learning interface containing training materials and consisting of 7 modules (available in 7 languages: EN, PL, LT, ES, GR, PT, SK):

1.	Digital start-ups vs Digital scale-ups
2.	Circular economy in your start-up
3.	Digital Lifestyle Entrepreneurship
4.	Internet of Things in entrepreneurial practice
5.	Infrastructure of sensors in daily business usage
6.	Analytics Algorithms for Customers Big Data
7.	Cybersecurity in your start-up.

results.resultDescription: This is a report that provides specific information about the best practices and technologies realized in the project partner countries, adaptable to the MILAN project. Partners conducted case studies of modern vocational training in the field of professions for advanced manufacturing systems. The analysis is multi-pronged. The report contains the most interesting examples and analyzes regarding robotics and automation in projects leading to the implementation of the idea of Industry 4.0.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultDescription: This document presents a program of robotics and automation courses for the implementation of the idea of Industry 4.0, developed as one of the results of the MILAN project. The developed curriculum consists of 4 blocks of 10 thematic modules, several lessons in each. It is built in such a way that selected parts can be used without losing the quality of the training. The topics of individual modules were matched to the needs of people already employed in SMEs or learning at vocational schools. It is shown where to use virtual and augmented reality technologies in order to increase the attractiveness and effectiveness of education. (Polish language version)

results.resultDescription: This is the content of the MILAN training courses in the scope of Advanced Manufacturing i.e. robotization and automation for the implementation of Industry 4.0. Under the four blocks, the training content of the 10 modules have been developed consisting of 27 lessons in total. For each lesson, a handbook has been prepared. It includes the introduction, lesson objectives, lesson content, assignment, examples and resources for further study, self-check questions and references.The aim is to equip target groups with the necessary e-learning materials and today's VR/AR tools to acquire the most effective way skills and knowledge to implement and use innovative automation and robotic-based technologies int everyday work life. (Polish language version)

results.resultTitle: Manual How to learn in the clouds
results.resultDescription: The project team, coordinated by GAIA, produced a documentary of the project. It gives you an explanation of the project and the chance to get impressions of the practical work done with children.
results.resultCategory: Dissemination material
results.resultType: Description of the project (PPT, pdf, Prezi...)

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_1_Video_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

The first educational box worked with the topic of video making. The aim was to teach kids and young adults how to use mobile devices and computers as well as to understand the functionality of these devices and make use of the internet in order to solve tasks.

The box itself includes the challenge for kids to create a storybook, take pictures and videos, edit them to short videos, do interviews and encouraged the students to improve interpersonal competencies when introducing how to give constructive feedback
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_2_IT101_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

In our daily lives digital literacy is becoming the main transversal skill that every person needs to have. For this reason we prepared tasks for the children in which they playfully developed an understanding and skills in the field, e.g. knowledge on how a computer is assembled, first programming skills, how to use  different online services and for which purposes.

To do so the IT 101 Box includes tasks such as assembling and connecting a Raspberry Pi, connecting to WiFi, using Google applications and other online platforms, understanding and making folder systems, writing letters, using the calculator, do’s and don’ts of the internet or using Scratch.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_3_English_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

In the initial needsassessment knowledge of English was identified as a transversal competence that could support the children and youth in their future. For this reason the English box includs various activities and materials to develop and  improve English language skills, as well as interest, starting at the very basics: spelling, pronounciation and how to make a sentence. For more advanced children other tasks were created, including tasks with the aim to construct family trees, record messages with mobile devices and to discuss about “big questions” of general education.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_4_Programming_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

Already as part of the IT 101 box children started to develop first programming skills. This box allows them to become more confident and to deepen their knowledge and skills. The box is divided into four parts, working with MaKeyMaKeys, Minecraft, Ozobots and WeDos.

Students take part in hands-on programming and engineering activities, get to understand the electric circuits and engage in handicraft work – e.g students develop banana pianos (see picture). By working with the included materials, the programming box aims at triggering and fostering students’ creativity, logical and computational thinking skills as well as problem- solving competencies.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_5_ekopolis_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

Based on the fact that environmental education was one of the fields that both teachers and youth workers unexceptionally wanted to cover within the project, the Ekopolis box provided children and youth with the opportunity to do so. Ekopolis is a board game developed by the project partner SCIO. It playfully teaches young people about ecology and sustainable cities and towns. At the same time the box introduces kids to many new ecological and urban space concepts as well as related english vocabulary.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
https://brainsintheclouds.eu/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/EN_publication_6_reallife_mit_IV_ohne_QR.pdf

The development and materials of the Real Life Box were based on the feedback from children, youth, parents, local stakeholders, teachers and youth workers with regards to to the work done until then. The tasks were designed to fit the needs of the children and youth in fields that have been observed as challenges. Activities of this box include Rom a culture, history, customs and traditions, personal hygiene, functioning of different relationships, repairing stuff, first aid, going on a trip, how to behave in a restaurant etc. The activities demand and foster creativity, teamspirit, sensitivity to others and communication skills.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: Context Study of Tracking Systems and Measures
results.resultDescription: The context study compiles the various tracking systems and measures at VET provider level in the seven countries of the ON TRACK  transnational partnership. It provides a comprehensive in-depth analysis of context, needs and challenges in the partner countries as well as. For the transnational context study each country provided a national report with an overall national context, various challenges and needs of the country, a mapping of tracking measures at VET provider level, a comprehensive description of one or more tracking measures and a specific case study of one national VET provider. The national level covers different measures or practices that are in place for tracking VET graduates (even if they are not systematic or comprehensive), available administrative data, that can be used for tracking, some quality assurance practices and the existing ‘quality culture of the country’s VET system and the VET provider, as well as different organizational capacities and IT competences.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultDescription:
The  technical manual aims to provide technical guidance to VET providers that want to design and establish a VET graduates tracking system, based on On Track methodology and using the model surveys. The technical manual complements the Methodological guide and deals only with the technical aspects on how to adapt the model surveys.
The technical manual consists of three different parts:
Part 1 includes instructions on how to use and adapt the Google survey tools
Part 2 includes instructions on how to use and adapt Limesurvey tools
Part 3 provides the three model questionnaires that are the basis of On Track surveys. One questionnaire for tracking graduates level 2-3, one for level 4-5 and one for level 6-7.
The manual provides all the technical information that a VET provider will need, in order to use On Track tools, how to adapt the surveys, how to invite responders and how to analyze the results.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: Chapter II. Report on Innovative pedagogies, methods and teaching skills for SCL
results.resultDescription: This study supply readers and other interested parties with innovative pedagogies in students-centered learning, methods, tools and teaching skills suitable for BEE education (Business, Engineering & Entrepreneurship). It provides modern techniques that cover most of the aspects of learning, focusing on the direct interaction between teacher and learners during classes. Still though, these methods may be utilized for online courses in distance learning.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultDescription: This executive summary elaborated in Romanian language by Romania project partners provides readers with ten principles that guide the student – centered learning pedagogies, and entails two improvement proposals for SCL approach in Business & Engineering, Entrepreneurship educational areas.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultDescription: This executive summary elaborated in Slovakian language gained by project partners from Slovak Republic provides readers with innovative pedagogies, teaching and learning skills, tools, and methods, and useful improvement proposals to be used by teachers and experts which adopt the student-centered practices within Business & Engineering, Entrepreneurship educational areas.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector
