results.resultDescription:
The three “CO” (Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness) Winter School (3COWS) is the first intensive programme for higher education learners and teaching staff extending the community of the Central European Functional Programming (CEFP) summer school in the frame of the ERASMUS+ project No. 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 “Focusing Education on Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness of Working Software” that was held between 22 and 26 January 2018.

The included material was created and presented in the frame of the above mentioned project.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
Zimska škola 3CO o kompatibilnost, razumljivost i ispravnost (3COWS: Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness) je prvi intenzivan program za učenike i nastavno osoblje visokog obrazovanja koji šire zajednicu ljetne škole Centralno-europskog funkcionalnog programiranja (eng. Central European Functional Programming, CEFP) u okviru ERASMUS + projekta Br. 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 pod naslovom "Fokusiranje obrazovanja na kompatibilnost, razumljivost i ispravnost radnog softvera" koji se održava od 22. do 26. siječnja 2018. godine.


Uključeni materijal izrađen je i predstavljen u okviru navedenog projekta.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
Трите зимни училища „CO“ (Компонируемост, разбираемост и коректност) (3COWS) е първата интензивна програма за обучаващи се и преподаватели с висше образование, разширяваща общността на Централното европейско функционално програмиране (CEFP) в рамките на проекта ERASMUS + № 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 „Фокусиране на образованието върху комбинируемостта, разбираемостта и коректността на работния софтуер“, което се проведе между 22 и 26 януари 2018 г.

Включеният материал е създаден и представен в рамките на гореспоменатия проект.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
A három “CO” (Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness) téli iskola (3COWS) az első intenzív program felsőoktatási tanulók és tanárok számára a közép-európai funkcionális programozás (CEFP) nyári iskolája közösségének kiterjesztését célzó 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 számú “Focusing Education on Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness of Working Software” ERASMUS+ projekt keretében, amelyet 2018. január 22. és 26. között került megrendezésre.

A mellékelt anyagot a fenti projekt keretében hozták létre és mutatták be.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: Materiais escolares de inverno os três “Co”
results.resultDescription:
As três escolas de inverno “CO” (compostabilidade, compreensibilidade e correção) (3COWS) são o primeiro programa intensivo para alunos do ensino superior e professores que estendem a comunidade da escola de verão da Programação Central da Europa (CEFP), no marco do projeto ERASMUS + 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 “Focusing Education on Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness of Working Software”, realizada entre 22 e 26 de janeiro de 2018.

O material incluído foi criado e apresentado no quadro do projeto mencionado acima.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: MATERIAL DIDACTIC  PENTRU ŞCOALA DE IARNĂ THREE “Co”
results.resultDescription:
Școala de iarnă ”The three CO”  – Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness – abreviat 3COWS – este primul program intensiv dedicat participanților din sistemul universitar. Programul extinde activitățile comunității în jurul programelor CEFP – Central European Functional Programming – axat pe aplicarea programării funcționale și a fost organizat în perioada 22-26 Ianuarie 2018. Școala este organizat prin proiectul ERASMUS+ cu codul 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402, întitulat “Focusing Education on Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness of Working Software”.

Materialul prezentat este produs în cadrul proiectului menționat mai sus.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
Zimná škola tri “CO” (Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness Winter School, 3COWS) je prvým intenzívnym školením vysokoškolských študentov a pedagógov, ktorá rozširuje komunitu Central European Functional Programming (CEFP). Uskutočnila sa v rámci implementácie ERASMUS+ projektu číslo 2017-1-SK01-KA203-035402 s názvom “Focusing Education on Composability, Comprehensibility and Correctness of Working Software”, a to v období medzi 22. a 26. januárom 2018.


Materiály obsiahnuté v tejto publikácii boli vytvorené a prezentované v rámci vyššie uvedeného projektu.

results.resultTitle: Programming Robots with RobotC programming environment - A Practical Guide
results.resultDescription:
This is a teaching and learning resource intended to support extracurricular training courses in the area of Mobile Robotics. It is targeted at learners with some prior knowledge of programming. The resource includes tutorials, sample exercises and sample programs based on the Lego EV3 platform. It can be used to develop skills for controlling and programming mobile robots.
The following areas are covered:
•	Controlling the robot’s motors
•	Controlling the robot’s speed and position
•	Using sensors (touch sensor, ultrasonic and infrared sensors, light sensor)
•	Programming a robot to follow a line, a predefined route from point A to point B, or a map stored in the memory of the robot
•	Guidelines for organizing Robot Competitions among learners.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
This is a teaching and learning resource intended to support extracurricular training courses in the area of Physical Computing. It is targeted at secondary school learners with some prior knowledge of programming. Physical Computing links programming to electrical & mechanical engineering, allowing graphical computer interfaces to respond to human input or changes in the outside world through sensors and microcontrollers, and then transform this input into another form, such as an animation or control commands to equipment. The resource is based on the Python programming language and Raspberry Pi as the platform for physical computing. 
The following areas are covered:
-	First Steps in Python: Time Estimation Game
-	Communicating with the Physical World - Using LEDs
-	Lights, Sounds and Buttons 
-	Object-Oriented Programming in Python - Games with Pygame Zero
-	More about Objects and Pygame Zero
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription: This teaching and learning resource is focused on the use of the popular open-source platform Scratch for the development of animations and simple games. It is intended for learners without strong knowledge in STEM fields. It does not require prior programming experience and is suitable for absolute beginners who do not feel comfortable with textual programming languages. The resource is based on a block-based Educational Programming Language (EPL) allowing learners to develop simple computer games, animations and other digital artifacts in a very intuitive and visual way.

Този учебен ресурс използва програмния език Python. Избраната платформа за физически изчисления е Raspberry Pi.

results.resultDescription: Ресурсът предоставя знания и умения за използването на популярната платформа Scratch за разработване на анимации и прости игри. Той не изисква опит в програмирането и е подходящ за абсолютно начинаещи, които не се чувстват комфортно с текстови езици за програмиране. Използва се програмен език, базирани на визуални блокове (псевдокод), който позволява на ученици без задълбочени умения по програмиране да създават прости компютърни игри, анимации и други дигитални артефакти.

results.resultTitle: Roadmap for local goverment on managing migration and diversity_ENG
results.resultDescription:
The Road Map (RM) is the intellectual output O3 of the project MAMIDI and supports the enhancement of local government  representatives’ and employees’ (especially all of them who are expected to come to direct contact with migrants and/or have influence on managing migrants and diversity at the local level of governance) ability to carry out self-assessment of their current possibilities for managing migration and diversity and taking proactive measure for their implementation and use in the everyday working life. The RM can serve as the useful tool for anybody working with migrants. The Roadmap on migration and diversity management is available in 4 languages (English, Greek, Hungarian, and Slovak) and serves as the supplementary material for learning modules of the MAMIDI e-learning course.
The RM provides the basic navigational elements for its users to encouraged them to reflect and think over the migration from the personal as well as professional point of view.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: Report   on Identification and Anticipation of Future Skill Needs for Local Government in the Area of Migration and Diversity Management_ENG
results.resultDescription: During project preparation the preliminary analysis of local government training needs has been carried out. Nevertheless the more detailed analysis was required in order to assure better matching and anticipating local government training needs in the area of migration and diversity management in the future. It enables to design effective training and predict which skills are needed in tomorrow's services. The report assesses results of survey for identification and forecasts of future skills and training needs of local government employees using quantitative and qualitative surveys. Based on the Guidelines for identification and forecasts of future skill needs, questionnaires for local government employees, semi-structured interviews  and focus group sessions with a group of migrants have been selected as appropriate methods for data collection. The Report is available in 4 languages (English, Slovak, Hungarian, Greek).
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultTitle: Module I: 	Cultural Manifestation and Acculturation which covers cultural aspect of migration_ENG
results.resultDescription:
The ERASMUS+ project  ”Managing Migration and Diversity through Local Government Capacity Building - MAMIDI”, aims to build capacity of local governments in order to be better prepared for the changes coming from present challenges of EU. The capacity will be enhanced by two main tools:
	Preparation and pilot run of the training course for local government.
	Roadmap for managing migration and diversity for local government.

The Course: Managing Migration and Diversity consists of four Modules:
Module I: 	Cultural Manifestation and Acculturation which covers cultural aspect of migration.
Module II: 	Local Integration Policy which covers social aspect of migration.
Module III:	Governance of Migration and Diversity at Local Level: Public Decision-Making which covers administrative aspect of migration. 
Module IV:	Discovering of migrants and refugees' economic potential which covers economic aspect of migration.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
Talented Europe web platform has being created using the software architectural pattern Model‚ View,  Controller (MVC). It divides a given software application into three interconnected parts, so as to separate internal representations of information from the ways that information is presented to or accepted from the user.

This result will generate the code and a cross browser web application being careful with user interface and conforming to the style guides for all the cross-plattform applications. Due to this, this result includes aspects such as web design, web publishing, web programming, and database management. The link of the web application is:

https://talentedeurope.eu

There is  a login/registration section, in the same way as traditional sites. Once logged into, a contextual side menu is presented to the user, in order to select the desired action. Depending on the profile of the logged user (company, student or institution) several options will be displayed.

It is well known that apps (mobile applications) are getting a huge relevance in modern software. The growth of mobile devices and its accessibility to the personal user market have changed the way the software was understood.

This result consists on the source code and mobile applications of Talented Europe application. These apps are implemented for the two most extended operative systems in mobile devices: Android and iOS. Although the source code of both applications can share the same design principles, it is clear that the programming languages are different. Android will be developed using Java and iOS will be developed using Swift.

In Android it is possible to find the app searching Talented Europe in the play store or following:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.talentedeurope.app

In iOS it is possible to find the app searching Talented Europe in the App store or following:

https://itunes.apple.com/es/app/talented-europe/id1294042608?mt=8

results.resultDescription:
INNOSOC 2016 Report: joint report with studies O1/A1 and O2/A1.

[O1/A1] A (yearly) study that identifies new ICT trends which emerged during the last year. The study took a twofold perspective on ICT and analyzed not only innovations that happened within ICT, but as well as how ICT fostered innovations in other fields (e.g., "green energy", "smart transport" or "inclusive society"). 

[O2/A1] A (yearly) study uses frames of "Europe 2020" and "Horizon 2020" programs to identify major societal challenges which emerged during the last year. 

INNOSOC 2016 Report is available at the INNOSOC webpage as well: http://sociallab.fer.hr/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/INNOSOC-2016-Report.pdf, and it was distributed to all participants of INNOSOC Multiplier Events and INNOSOC Workshops on INNOSOC USB sticks.

results.resultDescription: Einheitliches methodisch-didaktisches Konzept des Blended-Learning-Kurses Falinar, das als Grundlage für den Aufbau der drei Module mit den tourismusrelevanten Aspekten der Medizin, Sicherheit und Umwelt gilt. In den weiterführenden Übungen soll das im Grundmodul erworbene Wissen vertieft werden. Hier sind auch die Übungen zur interkulturellen Kompetenz angesiedelt.
Aufbauend auf den Kann-Fertigkeiten laut EU-Referenzrahmen auf Niveau B2 wird die Übungstypologie, auf der der BL-Kurs basiert, als Grundlage dargestellt.

Quize umfassen die Űbungen zu Hotspots in der kulturellen Kommunikation, zu den Modulen Medizin, Sicherheit und Umwelt und sprechen alle Partnerländer des Projektes an. Sie dienen als Einstieg in den Kurs, der Förderung der interkulturellen Kompetenz und sind unter https://falinar.tuke.sk/moodle/local/staticpage/view.php?page=quiz zu finden.

results.resultTitle: Sprachcurriculum zu Medizin, Sicherheit und Umwelt
results.resultDescription: Das neue Sprachcurriculum reagiert auf den bislang vorhandenen Sprachsylabus zu den tourismusrelevanten Aspekten der Medizin, Sicherheit und Umwelt und wurde laut EU-Sprachreferenzrahmen auf dem Sprachniveau B2 konzipiert.
Der Youtube Kanal Falinar wurde mit der Lernplattform verbunden, um dort die Videos abzuspeichern. Er ist unter https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCWuwKfOGrkpuabN4xsaMa6A zu finden.

results.resultTitle: Blended-Learning-Deutschkurs mit 3 Modulen auf der Lernplattform Moodle
results.resultDescription:
Der Blended-Learning-Kurs umfasst 3 Module zu den tourismusrelevanten Aspekten: Medizin, Sicherheit und Umwelt mit den für den Kurs erstellten 13 Einheiten mit insgesamt 256 Online-Übungen, 83 Präsenz-Übungen, 77 Audios, 2 Videos und vielen zusammenhängenden Links.
Der ganze Kurs mit allen Modulen steht online zur Verfügung und ist zu finden unter: 
MEDIZIN –  https://falinar.tuke.sk/moodle/course/index.php?categoryid=2
UMWELT – https://falinar.tuke.sk/moodle/course/index.php?categoryid=3 
SICHERHEIT – https://falinar.tuke.sk/moodle/course/index.php?categoryid=4

Die Projektwebseite Falinar wurde erstellt, um den ganzen Blended-Learning-Deutschkurs auf der Lernplattform präsent zu machen. Ausserdem bietet die Seite der breiten Öffentlichkeit auch Kontakinformationen über Projektpartner, Disseminationen, aktuelle Beiträge usw. auf ihrer externen Seite. Für die Zwecke der Projektarbeit wurde die interne Seite (Projektcloud) erstellt, um die Kommunikation und Dokumentation zwischen den Projektpartnern effektiv zu gestalten.

08b1f819-79d1-4051-8dcc-427db4e09e84.projectTags: Disabilities|New learning and teaching methods and approaches|Inclusion, promoting equality and non-discrimination
08b1f819-79d1-4051-8dcc-427db4e09e84.projectLevel2Label: Partnerships for cooperation and exchanges of practices
08b1f819-79d1-4051-8dcc-427db4e09e84.projectDescriptionObjectives: The lack of access to suitable assistive technologies that meet their specific needs perpetuates the difficulties faced by people with disabilities (PwD) to achieve their autonomy and participate in society. To transform this, Design2Freedom proposes to raise awareness among students to place PwD at the center of the design process, by promoting the transversal incorporation of Person-Centered Design in university curricula.
08b1f819-79d1-4051-8dcc-427db4e09e84.projectDescriptionImplementation: Design2Freedom proposes to use participatory and inclusive methodologies for teaching Person-Centered Design, promoting collaboration between higher education and social organizations, and involving PwD throughout the process. Training actions will be carried out for the partners, based on which each university will pilot with its students. The generated knowledge will feed into the intellectual outputs that will be exploited through multiplier events in each country.
08b1f819-79d1-4051-8dcc-427db4e09e84.projectDescriptionResults: The intellectual outputs of the project will be collected in the Design2Freedom Educational Platform, which will contain: a MOOC course, a Good Practice Guide collecting the process, a Toolkit, and a Map of existing experiences. These outputs will be useful for the entire educational community, social organizations, public bodies, and social enterprises. The project aims to create a culture of Person-Centered inclusive design in education, which will allow building a more inclusive society.

b3960aa0-2378-4e69-9964-d3da25e63909.projectDescriptionObjectives:
CURATE will combine AI solutions related to the entrepreneurial process to develop an incubator programme that will provide migrant students with a challenge-based platform to better meet their learning styles and provide transferable forward-looking skills. 

CURATE will actively engage those from the world of work to become key catalysts in the codesign of new learning and teaching practices with the aim of providing solutions to real world challenges presented by labour market actors
b3960aa0-2378-4e69-9964-d3da25e63909.projectDescriptionImplementation:
4 codesign activities based on the cooperation of 5 HEIs and 18 APs, CURATE will implement a functional incubator programme CIP, that will be piloted by an international group of 75+ migrant students.
 
CURATE will host 2 virtual reverse pitching session, 2 F2F bootcamps as part of an innovative blended incubator framework and a full 16 week virtual incubator curriculum. 
1 MOOC, 5 webinars and a blended job/intern fair will share results and raise awareness of the inclusion of migrant students.
b3960aa0-2378-4e69-9964-d3da25e63909.projectDescriptionResults:
CURATE will bring together 75+ migrant students from an array of backgrounds and provide them the platform to tackle current challenges and through their diversity, provide solutions. 

Develop a student centred, challenge based curricula based on the adoption of AI solutions in entrepreneurship and promote a genuine interest in entrepreneurship through exposure to real world challenges and international collaboration gained through participation in the blended CURATE Incubator programme.

6d7ed0a3-0d08-4028-a20a-db0a701d33df.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The project aims at the following specific objectives:

- To review and update the curriculum of HR professionals at European level, by integrating knowledge and skills related to diversity management in the workplace
- To develop a VET course provides HR managers with the knowledge and tools necessary to understand and adequately address the needs of different age groups
- To promote the diffusion of best practices related to age management and the development of inclusive business strategies
6d7ed0a3-0d08-4028-a20a-db0a701d33df.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The following activities will be carried out:

- comparative analysis of existing qualifications
- preliminary survey among professionals, experts and external stakeholders
- joint staff training event in Greece
- delivery of pilot courses in partners’ Countries
- Short-term mobility of learners in Italy
- comparative analysis of current policies
- research of best practices at national and European level
- organisation of thematic round tables
- multiplier events in partner Countries
6d7ed0a3-0d08-4028-a20a-db0a701d33df.projectDescriptionResults:
The IMAGE partners will cooperate to produce a wide range of concrete results under an extensive and integrated approach, which will generate an impact on different levels and target groups. The main tangible results envisaged are:

- Updated description of the HR manager professional profile
- Blended training course targeted to HR managers
- Guidelines for the development of inclusive business strategies in HR management
- Comparative analysis of current policies
- Policy recommendations

599ea426-c0ad-45b6-91a7-38d2500fc975.projectDescription: The project stems from the clearly identified needs of young, unestablished artists in the field of contemporary visual and intermedia art in Slovenia and Slovakia. We are trying to provide young ...
599ea426-c0ad-45b6-91a7-38d2500fc975.projectTags: Creativity, arts and culture|Democracy and inclusive democratic participation|Green skills
599ea426-c0ad-45b6-91a7-38d2500fc975.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The main activities of the project are youth exchanges with Slovenian and Slovakian youth groups, which will take place in Ljubljana in August and in Košice in 2027. Before the exchange begins, preparatory activities will take place in each country (calls for participants, first group meeting, and preparation for the exchange). The youth exchange focuses on the themes of sustainability, reuse, physicality, and attitudes towards living, and provides a supportive and safe environment for young people to explore these concepts through artistic practices under the guidance of experienced mentors. After the exchange, we plan to organise several follow-up activities, primarily focused on showcasing the results of the exchange—artistic products made by young people from recycled materials. 
The first exchange allows young people to connect, get to know each other, form a group, and create a safe space in which they can explore, ask questions, and experiment. The first exchange concludes with the presentation of the finished products in a curated exhibition. After the exchange, young people continue to work and develop their own skills and knowledge of sustainable practices in their local environment. 

In addition, they will prepare content in their local environments that they want to present to each other at the next youth exchange, work on strengthening the acquired competences, test approaches and materials, and explore various techniques and methods, which they will then share with each other at the exchange in Slovakia. 
The second exchange in Slovakia is crucial, as it allows young people to show what they have done, to present their knowledge and skills to their peers, and to gain more responsibility and autonomy to set their own program based on the identified needs and interests of the group. In this way, the entire project follows the logic of increasing the participation of the young people involved, as it gradually prepares them to develop and test their new skills in various fields or put them into practice immediately. 
Approximate schedule of activities:
July 31–August 10, 2026 Reciklar art colony in Ljubljana (SK, SI)
February 22–26, 2027 Reciklar art colony in Košice
599ea426-c0ad-45b6-91a7-38d2500fc975.projectDescriptionResults:
The most ostensible result of the youth exchange will be the artistic products that will be created during the art colony and will be on display both in the Alkatraz Gallery and at the premises of the Faculty of Arts in Košice, Slovakia. Since both the AKC Metelkova and the premises of the Faculty of Arts themselves are highly frequented and a diverse profile of people come there on a daily basis, the visibility of the young people's production will be considerable. In this way, we would like the results to be available even after the end of the exchange itself, and they will also become part of the artistic portfolio of the participants.

 As a long-term effect, we would like to establish a model of connection between non-governmental and public institutions, between different public spaces, which can be both faculties and alternative spaces, and which serve as inspiration for further creation and cooperation.

 The model of this cooperation will also be presented within the framework of the regular study process at the Faculty of Arts: in this way, it will be ensured that future generations of young artists are also introduced to ways of creation that may not be obvious to everyone.

 Close cooperation in the collective process will ensure that young people gain experience of working and collaborating, not only in a local but also in an international context, which for artists is often quite individual and less group-based.

 To ensure the lasting effects of the project, we will establish several substantive, structural and partnership mechanisms in the planning and implementation phase, which will enable continued work even after the formal conclusion of the youth exchange. One of the desired results is also the establishment of an informal network of young artists, which will enable further networking, sharing opportunities (calls, residencies, exhibitions) and the development of self-initiated collaborations. We will encourage participants to form joint project ideas and support each other.

 We will include the developed working methods (connecting artistic practice, sustainability and informal learning) in the regular programs of both organisations and use them as a model for working with other target groups.

 Our wish is that such international collaborations of young artists and youth exchanges become part of regular practice.

 During the project, we will also develop ways and methods of working for young people with fewer opportunities, which we will then use in the planning of future projects, thereby expanding access to international programs for young people with fewer opportunities in the long term.

b7b2c1e3-d00f-40b8-b7f6-c692bfd4e375.projectTitle: Immersive VR Experience for International Mobility

b7b2c1e3-d00f-40b8-b7f6-c692bfd4e375.projectDescriptionBackground: We applied for the READY, IMMERSE AND GO! project in order to address a major strategic challenge shared by the entire partnership: strengthening the attractiveness and accessibility of international mobility in higher education, while taking into account the profound transformations brought about by the health crisis and the digital transition. Within our institutions, we had observed a significant decline in students’ willingness to engage in international mobility, particularly among the most vulnerable learners. Many experienced a lack of confidence, an increased fear of the unknown, and difficulties in envisioning themselves in an international experience. This situation was further exacerbated by socio-economic, cultural, or health-related factors, which continued to hinder equitable access to international mobility. At the same time, we identified virtual reality as an emerging technology with strong educational potential and as a powerful psychological support tool, which remains largely underexplored in the context of preparation for international mobility. It was within this framework that the partnership decided to experiment with an innovative approach combining virtual reality, student co-creation, and pedagogical ing
b7b2c1e3-d00f-40b8-b7f6-c692bfd4e375.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The main objective of the READY, IMMERSE AND GO! project was to experiment with the use of virtual reality as an innovative pedagogical tool to prepare students, trainees, and apprentices for international mobility.
More specifically, the project aimed to:
1. Strengthen learners’ confidence and motivation when preparing for a stay abroad. By offering realistic immersive experiences, the project sought to help students overcome their fears (fear of the unknown, culture shock, isolation, language barriers) and to envision themselves more confidently in an international mobility experience.
2. Promote inclusion and equal opportunities by providing a first “virtual international experience” to individuals who, for social, economic, or health-related reasons, do not have easy access to physical mobility.
3. Contribute to the digital transformation of higher education. By testing virtual reality in a new field of application (international mobility), the partnership aimed to produce transferable results for other institutions and to enrich innovative teaching practices.

In the longer term, the project ultimately aimed to increase the number of participants in international mobility programmes.
b7b2c1e3-d00f-40b8-b7f6-c692bfd4e375.projectDescriptionImplementation:
Within the framework of the READY, IMMERSE AND GO! project, we implemented the following activities:
1. A co-creation exercise with students to directly involve end beneficiaries. Groups of students who had already experienced international mobility were engaged to identify the most challenging situations encountered during a stay abroad, define the key skills required to address them, and prioritise the scenarios to be recreated in virtual reality.
   The outcomes of this collaborative work were formalised in a compendium, which served as the foundation for the pedagogical and technical design of the immersive content.
2. Design and development of the virtual reality platform. Based on the results of the co-creation phase, the partnership designed and developed a VR platform integrating immersive scenarios replicating real-life international mobility situations, as well as interactive activities (micro-challenges and practical exercises).
3. Piloting, dissemination, and exploitation. This phase included pilot testing with students, collection of user feedback, iterative improvement of the tools, and dissemination of user feedback, iterative improvement of the tools, and dissemination of the results to the academic community.
b7b2c1e3-d00f-40b8-b7f6-c692bfd4e375.projectDescriptionResults:
1. Creation of a compendium resulting from student co-creation: A first major achievement was the development of a pedagogical compendium, produced through co-creation workshops with students who had already experienced international mobility. This compendium served as a shared reference for the entire partnership in the design of the immersive content.
2. Development of a virtual reality platform dedicated to mobility preparation: The project enabled the design and implementation of a VR platform integrating immersive scenarios replicating real-life international mobility situations, interactive activities (micro-challenges and practical exercises), and additional VR resources.
3. Pilot phase and iterative improvement: User testing confirmed the relevance of virtual reality as a psychological and pedagogical preparation tool for international mobility.
4. Dissemination and exploitation of results: The partners carried out several dissemination activities, including presentations within their institutions, sharing results with the academic community, mobilisation of existing international networks, and awareness-raising among staff involved in mobility.

806f2cfa-6f13-4011-97a1-541d6f94e245.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The UlySA 4 Society project is designed as the logical next step to the UlySA Boot Camp project. Through the UlySA Boot Camp project we promoted European Union, European values, European Citizenship among UlySA group of young participants. The UlySA 4 Society exchanges project will bring again the UlySA young participants together to encourage them to take concrete action through social projects using all the knowledge and skills developed during the non formal education activites of the UlySA Boot Camp.

After increasing their awareness and knowledge on "Youth Voice" on European policies and how they can concretely impact them, the UlySa 4 Society project will focus on how young participants can actually be Change Makers; how they can be "European values promotors" , how they can impact their community and their local territory.

The project aims to create a sense of belonging among the participants so they can feel that they belong to the same community, and they can have an impact in the Ulysseus Alliance but also outside the Alliance. The objectives of UlySA 4 Societry are to learn young participants about how European Union integrates Global Challenges and SGD into its policies and how Young participants can be active european citizens and help solve global challenges at local and/or european level. This project aims to develop better understanding of SGD and Global challenges and how they impact local territory and local communities. To reach those goals specific focus will be done on Intercultural competence, collaborative competence, peer learning and peer mentoring competence. Young participants will learn that global challenges should be solve at international level gathering skills and expertise from different country, different culture, different social and environmental background.

The main activity of the project is a 5 days Exchange mobility in Nice (France). One of the main deliverables of the UlySA 4 Society  is a concrete UlySA 4 Society Development Plan with concrete and specific social and/or environmental projects to be carried out by the UlySA young participants in 2026/2027 academic year.
806f2cfa-6f13-4011-97a1-541d6f94e245.projectDescriptionImplementation:
28 young participants (from 18 to 26 years old) will be directly involved in the project. They come from 6 European countries (France, Italia, Germany, Spain, Austria and Slovakia) and from 1 non associated Erasmus + partner country (Montenegro). The fact that the young participants come from 6 different countries strongly contributes to the inclusion and diversity dimension of the
project.
The UlySA 4 Society project will last twelve months and will be divided in four different phases:

- First phase: One online meeting in May 2026 to finalize the last logistical and organizational aspects of the UlySA 4 society exchange mobility
Participants: 4 young participants per institution means 28 participants in total.
Duration of the online meeting: 2 hours

- Second phase: a self-paced MOODLE module will be accessible to the young participants from the online meeting until the on-site activity in July in Nice
Participants: 4 young participants per institution means 28 participants in total.
Duration: between 4 and 6 weeks

- Third phase: The UlySA 4 Society exchange mobility: 5 days mobility in Nice at Université Côte d'Azur, from June 29th  to July the 3rd 2026.
Participants: 4 young participants per institution means 28 participants in total (+ 7 leaders (one per group) + 2 facilitators)
Duration: 5 days (excluding travel days)
Location: In the premises of Université Côte d'Azur, Nice, France

- Fourth phase: online meeting with all the participants to reflect on the impact of the exchange mobility experience and to discuss the UlySA 4 Society Development plan 2026-2027  Participants: 4 young participants per institution means 28 participants in total.
Duration of the online meeting: 2 hours
806f2cfa-6f13-4011-97a1-541d6f94e245.projectDescriptionResults:
The project targets several key results:
- Increased awareness among Young participants on Sustainable Development Goals and Global Challenges and how they have concrete impact at local level
-Better understanding of how the European includes Sustainable Development Goals into its policies
-Better understanding of how the European policies give concrete tools and financial support to tackle Global Challenges
-Better understanding on how to use "Youth voice" at European level and how Young participants can become Change makers into their own community and own territory
-Creation of a network of different structures and institutions (Public authorities, Youth organisation, Secondary education institutions, Primary schools, EU representations in each participating countries)
-Development of personal and social skills: young participants will gain key life skills, including leadership, teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making. These are essential for personal development and active citizenship.
-Intercultural Competence: through direct exposure to different cultures, participants will develop a deeper understanding of cultural diversity, improving their ability to work and interact in multicultural environments. It helps foster tolerance, respect, and inclusion
-Stronger partnership: participants will build strong, lasting friendships with young people from different countries. These relationships will help the development of future collaboration on UlySA, fostering long-term intercultural exchange and cooperation.
The foreseen impact of the project is to reinforce the participation of young people into Ulysseus and society so they can become “leaders of change” in their institution and territory.

fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectDescription: Our main goal in implementing this project was to significantly increase the internationalisation of our students and staff. We focused on providing valuable opportunities to gain international ex...
fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectTitle: Mobility of higher education students and staff supported by internal policy funds (KA131-HED) - Coordinator: TECHNICKA UNIVERZITA V KOSICIACH
fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectLevel3Label: Mobility of higher education students and staff
fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectDescriptionObjectives:
Our main goal in implementing this project was to significantly increase the internationalisation of our students and staff. We focused on providing valuable opportunities to gain international experience that would help them develop intercultural competences, broaden their outlook and strengthen their professional networks across borders. By participating in Erasmus+ mobility, our students and staff were able to immerse themselves in different cultural and educational environments, enriching their understanding and approach to study/work.
In addition to individual development, we have sought to strengthen our university's overall ability to function effectively in a global context. By encouraging our students and staff to gain international experience, we have sought to foster more globally minded citizens, able to meet the challenges of an increasingly interconnected world. This project was a strategic initiative to ensure that our university remained competitive and innovative in an international environment, benefiting our students, staff and the wider community (city, region, Slovakia).
Despite the spill-over of the negative impacts of the pandemic period into this project, we are very pleased that we have been able to secure an increase over the previous project (2021) in all quantitative indicators. In this project we have successfully implemented: 351 mobilities (of which 250 staff mobilities), representing an increase of 90% of the total volume of mobilities, a 255% increase in staff mobility and a 13% increase in student mobility.
fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectDescriptionImplementation:
Throughout the year, we try to inform our students and staff about all the opportunities to go on different types of mobility within the Erasmus+ project. All offers are published on our main Erasmus+ page, where students and staff have their own dedicated section. Also, incoming offers from partners are forwarded to the faculties, where they are also shared directly on the faculty pages. Information about applying for a specific type of mobility, documents and all other important information such as what to do before, during and after the mobility can also be found on our website or given to students at our information sessions, which we organize for outgoing students (a separate session for both Slovak and foreign students of TUKE), as well as for incoming students. In addition to these meetings, we are available to them at any time by email, telephone or personal consultation. At the meetings with incoming students, we introduce them to the city of Košice, the university and slowly move on to more detailed information about the faculties, faculty coordinators, dormitories, activities offered by TUKE to students (sports, cultural), etc. In addition to the above mentioned meetings with outgoing and incoming students, we also have meetings with potential mobility applicants, where we explain what the Erasmus+ programme is, what needs to be done to apply for such mobility, we describe the whole process from application through nomination to acceptance at the university and signing the grant agreement. The grant agreement is signed by the students in person before they go on mobility and they are also presented with the Student Charter at this meeting. We are in contact with the students and we are ready to help them with even the smallest problem that arises (change of courses, accommodation problem, etc.). 
Staff attend information sessions directly at the faculty in cooperation with the faculty coordinator, but we are also available to them for personal consultations in case of any uncertainties (correct documents for a specific type of mobility, green transport, help in contacting the university, etc.). Within TUKE we also cooperate closely with student organizations ESN Košice, IAESTE and TUKE BEST.
fb72b042-1ed0-477f-a459-c384242a03b5.projectDescriptionResults:
Thanks to the Ulysseus Alliance of European Universities, we have sent many participants in this project on blended intensive programmes, which are becoming more and more popular among students. In total, we have sent our students to 8 BIPs in this project, both within the Ulysseus Alliance and beyond. In this project, we have increased the number of internship mobilities where 26 out of 30 expected mobilities have been realized and the interest was mainly for practical experiences in companies related to the students' field of study.
In the 2022 project we continued with the growing interest in staff mobility in both teaching and training. We sent 78 employees on teaching mobility and managed to send up to 172 employees on training mobility. In total, we have therefore carried out 250 staff mobilities involving academic, non-academic and research staff at TUKE. A large part of the mobilities were carried out at universities with which we have long-standing strong partnerships and research collaborations. The Ulysseus Alliance of European Universities has also had a major impact on staff mobility, thanks to which mobility is also increasing at our partner universities in France, Italy, Spain and Finland. In addition, many employees have also travelled for example to Portugal, Germany, Latvia and Greece.

12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectDescription: The Erasmus+ programme is a key instrument of the internationalisation strategy of the Technical University of Košice (TUKE) and plays an important role in the implementation of activities within ...
12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectTitle: Mobility of higher education students and staff supported by internal policy funds (KA131-HED) - Coordinator: TECHNICKA UNIVERZITA V KOSICIACH
12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectLevel3Label: Mobility of higher education students and staff
12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The Erasmus+ programme is a key instrument of the internationalisation strategy of the Technical University of Košice (TUKE) and plays an important role in the implementation of activities within the Ulysseus European University Alliance. TUKE’s participation in the programme demonstrates its strong commitment to fostering international cooperation, enhancing the quality of education, and expanding mobility opportunities for both students and staff. Through its involvement in the Ulysseus alliance, the university is building strategic partnerships with higher education institutions across and beyond the EU, thus creating space for synergies, resource sharing, and the promotion of innovation in education and research.
Within the framework of the 2023 project, we set an ambitious yet realistic goal – to carry out a total of 240 mobilities. A significant portion of these, specifically 110 mobilities, were allocated to students in order to support their international experience and increase their competitiveness in the labour market. Out of these, 80 mobilities were dedicated to study stays, allowing students to enhance their academic and language skills directly at partner universities, while 30 mobilities focused on traineeships, providing them with practical skills and valuable contacts in an international environment.
Equally important was the involvement of TUKE staff, for whom 130 mobilities were allocated. This included 80 training mobilities, enabling staff to gain new knowledge, share best practices, and implement innovative approaches in their work, and 50 teaching mobilities, which supported the exchange of expertise, the internationalisation of curricula, and the strengthening of cooperation with partner institutions.
In addition to individual mobilities, we also set the goal of organising three Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs), which combine virtual and physical mobility formats and promote collaboration in international teams.
In planning the project, we took into account the experience from previous years, when the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath led to reduced interest in international mobility, and the full allocation of grants could not be utilised. Therefore, in this call, we applied for a lower number of mobilities with the aim of focusing more on high-quality implementation and ensuring efficient use of available resources. This approach reflects TUKE’s strategic intent – to prioritise the qualitative benefits for students and staff, thereby contributing to the long-term sustainability and development of internationalisation activities.
12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectDescriptionImplementation:
At our university, the process of applying for an Erasmus+ mobility is comprehensively supported and accompanied throughout the entire year. Students and staff are provided with information about mobility opportunities through regular information sessions, individual consultations, and email communication.
All current Erasmus+ mobility offers are regularly published on our main Erasmus+ web page, where students and staff have their own dedicated sections. In addition, offers from partner universities are continuously forwarded to individual faculties. Information regarding how to apply for a specific type of mobility, required documents, as well as practical guidance before, during, and after the mobility, is available on the Erasmus web page or provided during information sessions organized for both outgoing and incoming TUKE students. Meetings for outgoing students are divided according to the type of participants (Slovak and international students). For incoming international students, we hold sessions at the beginning of the semester where we share all the necessary information about TUKE, introduce them to their faculty coordinators, and assign Slovak “buddies” to help them with better adaptation and orientation upon arrival.
In addition to group sessions, we provide individual support to students via email, phone, or personal consultations. During meetings with prospective applicants, we explain the Erasmus+ program in detail, the application process, the entire procedure from nomination to acceptance at the partner university, including the signing of the grant agreement. Students sign the grant agreement in person before departure, and during this meeting, the Student Charter is also presented to them. During the mobility, we remain available to students and address any issues that may arise, such as course changes or accommodation-related questions.
TUKE staff participate in information sessions directly at the faculty in cooperation with the faculty coordinator, and they also receive individual support for any specific questions – from correctly completing documents for a particular type of mobility, to questions about green travel, and assistance in contacting the partner university.
In this project period, we successfully completed 100 student mobilities out of the planned 110, achieving a fulfillment rate of 91%, and at the same time, we conducted 113 staff mobilities out of the required 130, reaching an 87% success rate in this category.
12db326f-6223-49b2-b1c6-d270c8dd07fd.projectDescriptionResults:
The project was implemented very efficiently and ran smoothly, with a high level of engagement from both students and staff. Almost all planned mobilities were carried out, and the project was successfully implemented with nearly full utilization of the allocated funds.
As part of this project, we successfully completed a total of 100 student mobilities and 113 staff mobilities, resulting in an overall success rate of 98.34%.
From a results perspective, the project is considered highly beneficial. The number of students participating in study mobilities increased significantly, strengthening the international dimension of education and providing students with valuable academic and personal development opportunities. In addition, student traineeships were carried out, allowing participants to gain practical experience in international work environments.
Staff took part in both training and teaching mobilities, which supported their professional and academic development while also deepening cooperation with partner institutions. The project also included mobilities to third countries through International Credit Mobility (ICM), with three staff members from the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering successfully completing mobilities to India. This experience represents an important step toward developing non-European cooperation and opens new opportunities for future partnerships.
A significant achievement of the project was the organization of one Blended Intensive Programme (BIP) involving several partner institutions. This activity provided participants with a combined learning format, integrating both virtual and physical components, and promoted intercultural collaboration.
Overall, the project met expectations and made a strong contribution to achieving the institution’s strategic goals in the areas of internationalization, improving the quality of education, and developing human resources.

f1bb2a03-fa88-42c6-a771-ccad7f359b76.projectDescriptionObjectives: The Erasmus+ programme is an integral part of the internationalisation strategy of the Technical University of Košice (TUKE) and contributes significantly to the implementation of the Ulysseus project of the Alliance of European Universities. The fact that TUKE is actively involved in the Erasmus+ programme underlines its commitment to support international cooperation, promote international mobility and improve the overall quality of education. * In addition, the involvement in the Ulysseus Alliance demonstrates TUKE’s intention to build strategic partnerships with higher education institutions in the EU and beyond. TUKE strives to create synergies, share resources and promote innovation and excellence in education and research. * In the 2021 project, we aimed to increase the number of students and staff travelling on mobility, even though it was still partly a Covid period. The project foresaw 188 student mobilities and 20 mobility for internships. For staff mobility, 54 teaching and 31 training mobilities were foreseen. The launch of the Ulysseus Alliance was also linked to the plan to implement seven BIPs. Unfortunately, the impact of the Covid has made the implementation of the planned mobilities significantly more difficult.
f1bb2a03-fa88-42c6-a771-ccad7f359b76.projectDescriptionImplementation: We provide our students and staff with info about E+ mobility throughout the year in the form of info meetings, consultations and email communication. Detailed info is published on our website dedicated exclusively to E+ mobility. Info sessions are held for both outgoing and incoming participants, as well as for potential mobility applicants. For incoming students, the meeting includes info about TUKE, the city/region, the team of faculty coordinators, upcoming events at TUKE, ESN activities, etc. For future mobility participants the info session includes introduction of the advantages of participating in E+ mobility, presentations by E+ mobility former participants (sharing experiences) and discussion. Info sessions for staff are mostly carried out directly at the faculties in cooperation with the faculty coordinators. On our website, our students and staff can find all the info on how to prepare for mobility, what to do during mobility and what is needed for a successful completion of their mobility. We actively use EWP, BN, OLA and OLS in the administration of outgoing mobilities. After signing a contract (in person), the participant receives a grant. We monitor the mobility and check the documents and evaluate upon arrival.
f1bb2a03-fa88-42c6-a771-ccad7f359b76.projectDescriptionResults: Despite the fact that the 2021 project was largely affected by COVID-19, we were able to successfully send 186 participants on mobility, incl. participants in BIPs and ICM. We have been able to successfully expand the range of destinations for students and staff. The largest number of students went to IT, PT and Korea (ICM). Mobility with AT, ES and FR (staff) took off more intensively.   * Repeated emergencies, ongoing online teaching and travel constraints have greatly complicated the decision making process for our students to participate in mobility. Despite the large number of nominations, many students cancelled their mobility. Internships were cancelled by students mainly due to the online mode of work (they were not interested).  * On the other hand, staff showed a huge interest in E+ mobility immediately after the travel ban was relaxed, which was also due to the launch of many activities of the ULYSSEUS Alliance. TUKE used the pandemic period as an opportunity to adjust the internal rules for E+ mobility so that unused nominations could be used later.

5fbbe85b-d07e-4ebb-8ab7-258445ead7cc.projectDescription: The main objective of the UlySA Boot camp is to promote exchanges on the European Union, citizen participation and the impact of “youth voice” on European policies, particularly in terms of higher...
5fbbe85b-d07e-4ebb-8ab7-258445ead7cc.projectTags: Key competences development|Awareness about the European Union|Youth employability
5fbbe85b-d07e-4ebb-8ab7-258445ead7cc.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The main objective of the UlySA Boot camp is to promote exchanges on the European Union, citizen participation and the impact of “youth voice” on European policies, particularly in terms of higher education. The project aims to create a sense of belonging among the participants so they can feel that they belong to the same community, and they can have an impact in the Ulysseus Alliance but also outside the Alliance.  The objectives of UlySA Boot Camp are to learn young participants about how European Union works and how they can actively participate and influence European policy especially Higher education European policy through their European Universities Alliance Ulysseus. This project aims to develop understanding of participatory processes and their consequences for promoting active citizenship. It also encourages intercultural understanding and responsibility among young people by offering them opportunities for personal and professional development. 

The main activity of the project is a 5 days Boot Camp mobility in Kosice (Slovakia). One of the main deliverables of the Boot Camp is the UlySA Action Plan 2026-2027.
5fbbe85b-d07e-4ebb-8ab7-258445ead7cc.projectDescriptionImplementation:
20 young participants (from 18 to 26 years old) will be directly involved in the project. They come from 4 European countries (France, Spain, Austria and Slovakia) and from 1 non associated Erasmus + partner country (Montenegro). The fact that the young participants come from 5 different countries strongly contributes to the inclusion and diversity dimension of the project. 

 

The UlySA BOOTCAMP project will last twelve months and will be divided in four different phases: 

First phase: One online meeting in September to finalize the last logistical and organizational aspects of the Bootcamp 

Participants:  4 young participants per institution means 20 participants in total. 

Duration of the online meeting: 2 hours 

 

Second phase: a self-paced MOODLE module will be accessible to the young participants from the online meeting until the on-site activity in October in Kosice. 

Participants:  4 young participants per institution means 20 participants in total. 

Duration: between 4 and 6 weeks 

 

Third phase: The Boot camp:  5 days mobility in Kosice at the Technical university of Kosice, from 20th to 24th of October 2025. 

Participants: 4 young participants per institution means 20 participants in total (+ 5 leaders (one per group) + 2 facilitators) 

Duration: 5 days (excluding travel days) 

Location: In the premises of the Technical University of Kosice, Slovakia 

 

Fourth phase: online meeting with all the participants to reflect on the impact of the Bootcamp and to discuss the UlySA Action plan 2026-2027 to be delivered during the Bootcamp. 

Participants:  4 young participants per institution means 20 participants in total. 

Duration of the online meeting: 2 hours
5fbbe85b-d07e-4ebb-8ab7-258445ead7cc.projectDescriptionResults:
The project targets several key results: 
-Better understanding of the European Union structure and functioning 
-Better understanding of the European policies especially Higher education European policy 
-Emergence of young leaders capable of running and implementing a students association and capable of participating in decision-making at Ulysseus level.  
-Creation of a network of different structures and institutions (Public authorities, High schools, Primary schools, EU representations in each participating countries) 
-Development of personal and social skills: young participants will gain key life skills, including leadership, teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making. These are essential for personal development and active citizenship. 
-Intercultural Competence: through direct exposure to different cultures, participants will develop a deeper understanding of cultural diversity, improving their ability to work and interact in multicultural environments. It helps foster tolerance, respect, and inclusivity. 
-Stronger partnership: participants will build strong, lasting friendships with young people from different countries. These relationships will help the development of future collaboration on UlySA, fostering long-term intercultural exchange and cooperation. 

The foreseen impact of the project is to reinforce the participation of young people into Ulysseus activities and decision-making process and to develop and strengthen their soft skills such as interculturality, communication and problem-solving so they can become “leaders of change” in their institution.

4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectDescription: The aim was to expand and deepen cooperation in Regions 2 (Belarus, Ukraine), 3 (Egypt), 4 (Russia), and 10 (Venezuela) through academic exchange, capacity building, joint educational and research...
4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectTitle: Mobility of higher education students and staff supported by external policy funds (KA171-HED) - Coordinator: TECHNICKA UNIVERZITA V KOSICIACH (E10208611)
4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectLevel3Label: Mobility of higher education students and staff supported by external policy funds
4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectDescriptionObjectives: The aim was to expand and deepen cooperation in Regions 2 (Belarus, Ukraine), 3 (Egypt), 4 (Russia), and 10 (Venezuela) through academic exchange, capacity building, joint educational and research activities, and long-term partnerships with emphasis on quality, inclusion, and development support. Implementation was affected by external circumstances – the military conflict in Ukraine, political unrest in Venezuela, and, the withdrawal of 41% of mobilities from/to Egypt due to an error of the funding provider, (amendment to the Grant Agreement). TUKE reacted promptly by adjusting objectives and focusing on cooperation with Ukraine and Venezuela in technical sciences, ICT, civil engineering, energy, mechanical engineering, sustainable design, environmental engineering, academic freedom, and social responsibility. Cooperation with the Venezuelan university opened new opportunities in Latin America, particularly in geosciences and raw materials engineering. Staff mobility supported exchange of expertise and preparation of future student mobilities. Despite the withdrawal of Egypt, TUKE maintained its interest in cooperation with the Southern Mediterranean region and confirmed its commitment to develop partnerships beyond the project.
4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectDescriptionImplementation: Within the project, TUKE focused on cooperation with partner institutions in the regions of Eastern Partnership, Latin America, and the Southern Mediterranean (Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Venezuela, Egypt). After the outbreak of the military conflict, mobilities to Ukraine, Russia, and Belarus were suspended, which significantly affected the plans. Implementation was further challenged by post-COVID restrictions and administrative discrepancies that led to the removal of Egypt (41% of the original grant). Despite this, 30 mobilities (77% of approved) were successfully implemented. With Ukraine, we hosted 2 students and 24 staff and sent out 2 TUKE staff, with cooperation developing mainly with the universities: Sumy State (8), National Academy of Management – Kyiv (3), Uzhhorod National (11), and Lviv Polytechnic (6). Cooperation with Ukraine accounted for 93% of the total mobility volume, with 93% incoming mobilities seen as an important expression of solidarity and enrichment of TUKE’s academic environment. With Venezuela, two-way mobility was achieved (1 incoming, 1 outgoing), confirming mutual interest. Despite Egypt’s exclusion, initial contacts with a partner institution were established, with prospects for future cooperation.
4e27c035-71f1-44ea-9670-fccf89cdabe5.projectDescriptionResults: Despite restrictions in the first phase – more than 51% of the original grant could not be used due to the conflict in Ukraine and suspension of mobility to Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine – TUKE succeeded in meeting both quantitative and qualitative goals. In the second phase, we focused on strong support for Ukrainian students and staff (93% of mobilities), effectively using the remaining funds and strengthening cooperation with Ukrainian partners. We created conditions for continued academic collaboration, including future student exchanges, and established a partnership with a Venezuelan university, diversifying cooperation beyond the EU. Notable are the academic results with Ukraine in ventilation regulation, resulting in a joint publication and a lasting outcome for students. Valuable was also a TUKE staff mobility to the Central University of Venezuela with lectures and a field course for students, where a vision of long-term cooperation emerged, reinforced by a reciprocal visit of Dr. Rodriquéz to TUKE. The project proved that despite geopolitical challenges, mobilities have had a positive impact on students, internationalization, regional and national development, deeper partnerships, and crisis response.

9bde10be-d960-452a-826d-960199246105.projectLevel2Label: Partnerships for cooperation and exchanges of practices
9bde10be-d960-452a-826d-960199246105.projectDescriptionBackground: We applied for the Seniors Climate Action (SCA) project as a challenge to respond to the urgent need for climate awareness and digital inclusion among older generations. Seniors are often overlooked in climate debates and digital education, yet they hold valuable life experience, creativity, and social influence. Drawing on our previous experience in art and ecology, we identified a “white gap” where seniors were missing as active voices in cultural and environmental dialogue. Our motivation was not only to fill this gap, but also to share such expertise in this specific area with experts across Europe, contributing to the exchange of innovative practices. At the same time, we wanted to explore new ways of finding solutions through interdisciplinary art, creative communication, and multigenerational dialogue. The project responded by empowering seniors through artistic and educational activities linking climate change with cultural expression. By combining intergenerational learning, digital tools, and creative workshops, the partnership created space for seniors to become visible agents of change and to connect art, environment, and senior participation in an innovative European response.
9bde10be-d960-452a-826d-960199246105.projectDescriptionObjectives: The main objective of the Seniors Climate Action (SCA) project was to empower older generations to actively engage with climate change through creative, educational, and digital means. We aimed to address the exclusion of seniors from climate debates and digital environments by creating accessible opportunities for them to participate, learn, and share their perspectives. Building on our previous experience in art and ecology, we wanted to introduce innovative, interdisciplinary methods that connect environmental topics with artistic expression and cultural practice. Another objective was to foster intergenerational and creative communication, enabling younger and older participants to learn from one another and develop new forms of cooperation. We also wanted to strengthen climate and cultural education by creating activities in which seniors could take leadership roles as artists, learners, and communicators. Finally, we aimed to share this specific expertise with European experts, inspiring new approaches to inclusive climate action and sustainable education across borders.
9bde10be-d960-452a-826d-960199246105.projectDescriptionImplementation: The Seniors Climate Action (SCA) project was implemented through a diverse set of artistic, educational, and digital activities designed to engage seniors in climate awareness and creative expression. Partners organized workshops and seminars, creative events where seniors explored climate topics through visual arts, design, performance, and interdisciplinary practices. Intergenerational sessions brought seniors and students together, encouraging dialogue, knowledge exchange, and creative collaboration. A digital toolkit and online learning modules were developed to provide accessible resources, while the Kunstmatrix digital platform was used for a virtual gallery showcasing seniors’ artworks on climate and environment. Local and regional events, exhibitions, and fieldwork connected participants directly with their communities and environments, linking theory with practice. Multiplier events in partner countries provided opportunities to share outcomes with experts, educators, and stakeholders across Europe. Throughout the project, emphasis was placed on accessibility, inclusion, and innovation, ensuring seniors were empowered as active participants and communicators of climate action.
9bde10be-d960-452a-826d-960199246105.projectDescriptionResults: The project delivered a set of concrete outputs and demonstrable results. We produced the SCA Curriculum, detailing learning goals, competencies, session outlines, and facilitation guidance tailored for seniors and intergenerational groups. We launched the e-learning platform with structured units, videos, tasks, and downloadable materials that extend learning beyond workshops and ensure accessibility in different contexts. The SCA Toolkit - a practical collection of guides, exercises, and templates - supported educators and cultural workers in implementing activities. We curated the SCA online gallery on Kunstmatrix, showcasing artworks and creative interventions on climate themes, and staged physical and virtual exhibitions with strong local engagement. Evaluation instruments (questionnaires for seniors, artists, and educators) informed improvements and documented accessibility, usability, and satisfaction. Multiplier events disseminated outputs across Europe, strengthened professional networks, and increased seniors’ digital skills, confidence, and climate literacy. The project also fostered meaningful multigenerational dialogue, demonstrating that artistic and cultural approaches can inspire sustainable behaviours.

3. Policy recommendations for integrating climate neutrality training into higher education curricula. 
4. Increase collaboration between HEIs from 7 EU Mission cities.
5. An open-access digital manual, with training content & best practices. 
6. Increased awareness about climate-neutral cities.

91da5216-99eb-47cc-8644-09b8bb0659c2.projectDescriptionObjectives: The Robo STEM Academy project aims to utilize the potential of robots and STEM methodologies as educational and edutainment platforms to meet the new educational demands and boost STEM skills and competencies of VET students, teachers, and tech-groups. 91da5216-99eb-47cc-8644-09b8bb0659c2.projectDescriptionImplementation: The project will provide students and teachers with ready-made STEM projects and support tools that they can use for teaching and learning STEM subjects using robots. The team will create a web-based advanced game and jury for online international robo-STEM competitions, robo-STEM lessons and teachers toolkit, and robo-STEM edu-hub and community of practice to facilitate the educational innovations and the inclusive digital transformation in VET in BG, RO, SK and UA, and throughout the EU.
91da5216-99eb-47cc-8644-09b8bb0659c2.projectDescriptionResults: The project builds upon the partners' know-how and several success stories. Its results will equip teachers, trainers, and tech-communities with high-quality, ready-to-use edutainment robo-STEM content for classroom and extracurricular activities (incl. but not limited to VET), supported by a wide peer-network, as a sustainable environment for cooperation and co-creation. The project will provide valuable know-how in robo-STEM to the target groups in the partner countries and EU, and UA and MKD.

a00a34cc-a719-4f8b-b175-b03c2e988699.projectDescriptionObjectives: The BOOST IN project seeks to significantly elevate global competence among students and staff. Recognizing the digital age, BOOST IN aims to enhance digital skills and projects innovative internationalization methods creating a rich environment for cross-cultural learning and knowledge exchange. In essence, BOOST IN is a comprehensive initiative that aims to modernize higher education, equipping students and staff with the skills and experiences they need to thrive in a globalized world.
a00a34cc-a719-4f8b-b175-b03c2e988699.projectDescriptionImplementation: BOOST IN partners will co-create pedagogical content on global competence for students, administrative and academic staff in the form of micro-learning modules and micro-challenges. 44199746-f076-46d8-8044-d0dd84f6f483.projectDescriptionObjectives: METACOG strengthens AI literacy to tackle disinformation and fake news by fostering civic engagement and shared values in European societies. METACOG develops an AI literacy program to equip European citizens, particularly HEI students and teachers, with the capability to identify disinformation and fake news. The programme, equipped with relevant materials, innovative teaching methods, and best practices, acknowledges AI's dual role in both creating and countering disinformation and fake news.
44199746-f076-46d8-8044-d0dd84f6f483.projectDescriptionImplementation: METACOG will develop a practical AI literacy programme in an international consortium of students, teachers and MOOC users across 4 HEIs and 6 APs. Activities including a classroom programme, a MOOC, 4+ webinars, a teacher’s guide, a handbook, and a toolkit will be piloted and implemented with several other dissemination activities. These efforts are geared towards sharing outcomes and enhancing digital awareness on combating disinformation and fake news in European societies.
44199746-f076-46d8-8044-d0dd84f6f483.projectDescriptionResults: METACOG will develop an AI literacy taxonomy for using and creating reliable teaching material. The framework for teaching AI literacy in the context of disinformation will be developed. Central to our approach is the use of AI tools for disinformation detection, alongside an accessible MOOC, handbook, and toolkit for AI literacy in the context of disinformation detection. METACOG produces several other results including best practices, pilot cases, modular content design, and digital inclusion.
