1abfb0f8-a992-468a-ad32-9976b0675aba.projectDescriptionBackground: The main reason was the identified necessary changes in the way enterprises and universities operate and the desire to actively respond to these changes. The aim of our project is to fill the competence gap by developing and implementing educational programs that will focus on developing digital skills among students. We want to create programs that will not only provide theoretical knowledge, but also enable practical application of acquired skills in real projects. We want our students to become competitive on the labor market and be able to meet the challenges posed by the dark industrial revolution. The identification and preliminary research of industry needs conducted by the project team from Poland and Slovakia, as well as the analysis of available analytical data, indicate that among the long-term effects, analysts mention, among others, the widespread transition to so-called dark factories - fully automated, not requiring the presence of people or their negligible participation. The project team identified that despite the fact that young generations are growing up in the era of technology, many studies indicate insufficient digital and industry 4.0-related competences among students.
1abfb0f8-a992-468a-ad32-9976b0675aba.projectDescriptionObjectives: The main objective of the project was to improve the competences of a group of higher education staff from Poland and Slovakia. In addition, the main objective of the Project was to create a framework for education that would significantly improve the competences of higher education in the field of Industry 4.0, based on the experience and knowledge of international experts and practitioners of modern industry. The specific objectives of the Project are: improving the quality of education by developing international and innovative educational programs and a textbook, which will enable the transfer of the most up-to-date, comprehensive and practical know-how regarding solutions used in Indu. 4.0; expanding knowledge and promoting the concept of Industry 4.0 at universities; (3) strengthening cooperation between partner institutions in the field of shaping competences in the field of Industry 4.0 and increasing internationalization through the exchange of good practices and the development and dissemination of an innovative educational module, including educational programs and teaching materials. It was assumed that the implementation of the project would contribute to the increase in knowledge, skills and competences of students.
1abfb0f8-a992-468a-ad32-9976b0675aba.projectDescriptionImplementation: Firstly, as part of the project, 4 study visits were held in each of the partner countries combined with workshops. Secondly, 4 conferences were organised to disseminate the project results and promote the idea of ​​the fourth industrial revolution. In Poland, 2 stationary conferences were held, 1 conference in Slovakia and 1 online conference. Studies were conducted among students from Poland and Slovakia to determine their competences related to Industry 4.0 as well as personal and social competences. It should be emphasised that in order to increase the reach of surveys among students, the network of connections related to the functioning of the TOP500 Innovators association was used, among others. Research into the needs of the labour market in Poland and Slovakia was also conducted. Appropriate tools were developed to carry out these activities and after their completion, appropriate reports were developed. These materials formed the basis for developing profiles and profiles of graduates of first- and second-cycle studies in economics and technical fields, as well as profiles and profiles of graduates of the " Manager of Industry 4.0" postgraduate studies.
1abfb0f8-a992-468a-ad32-9976b0675aba.projectDescriptionResults: The project team developed the following: Report on the diagnosis of labor market needs in the context of ecological Industry 4.0, Balance of current competences of students of technical and economic fields in the field of ecological Industry 4.0 (Poland and Slovakia), Report on German experiences in the field of education in technical and economic fields in specializations related to ecological Industry 4.0, Report on the experience of the USA in the field of education in technical and economic fields in specializations related to ecological Industry 4.0, Innovative textbook for students of ecological Industry 4.0 and Ecological Industry 4.0 Manager, Case studies on the development of ecological Industry 4.0 in partner countries as future teaching material, Innovative textbook for students of ecological Industry 4.0 and Ecological Industry 4.0 Manager, Tool for conducting a balance of current competences of students of technical and economic fields in the field of ecological Industry 4 in the form of survey sheets with research, Tool for diagnosing labor market needs in the context of ecological Industry 4.0 in the form of surveys with research conducting research. Profiles and profiles of graduates of courses related toInustr 4.

results.resultTitle: Result 4 - Report - Experience  on Education for Green Industry 4.0 in Germany - english verion
results.resultDescription:
The report "Experience on Education for Green Industry 4.0 in Germany" provides a detailed overview of the education system in the field of Industry 4.0 in Germany, focusing on innovative approaches and educational practices. The document emphasizes the importance of ecological aspects in modern industry and highlights the key challenges faced by education in this area.

Particularly noteworthy are the interesting initiatives carried out at Technische Hochschule Wildau (TH Wildau), which aim to integrate sustainable development into their curricula. TH Wildau conducts various projects and courses that enable students to acquire the skills necessary to operate in a sustainable industry, combining theory with practical experience. The report serves as a valuable resource for educational institutions and companies looking to adapt their programs to meet the growing demands of Industry 4.0 in the context of environmental protection.
results.resultCategory: Scientific results (paper, study, report, analysis)

results.resultTitle: Result 12 - Experience on Education for Green Industry 4.0 in USA - english version
results.resultDescription:
The report titled "Experience on Education for Green Industry 4.0 in USA" presents the education system for youth and students in the United States, focusing on educational approaches related to Industry 4.0. In the first part of the document, various curricula and initiatives aimed at preparing students for work in modern, sustainable industries are discussed.

The report also highlights selected universities in the USA that offer innovative study programs closely aligned with the themes of Industry 4.0. Examples of programs and courses that integrate digital technologies, sustainable development, and practical skills are presented, enabling students to acquire the competencies necessary for success in a rapidly changing industrial environment. The document serves as a valuable resource for educational institutions and students interested in developing careers in the field of Industry 4.0.

results.resultTitle: Result 10 - Report- Labor markets needs - multilingual version
results.resultDescription:
Report on the diagnosis of labor market needs
in the context of ecological Industry 4.0. The authors of the report assumed that the competencies of a manager 4.0 and an engineer 4.0 consist of four basic components specialist-technical, personal, social and managerial competencies. However, these competencies were divided into two basic groups, 1) hard competencies, which include specialist-technical competencies and 2) soft competencies, which include personal, social and managerial competencies. Specialist-technical competencies are competencies related to specialist tasks for a given group of positions.

5092a6c5-e5f1-4e1e-b4b6-a7dd2f2af822.projectTags: Environment and climate change|Initial and continuous training for teachers, trainers and other education staff

5092a6c5-e5f1-4e1e-b4b6-a7dd2f2af822.projectDescriptionObjectives: Hi-EduCarbon course targeted for universities, state and public administrations and all private organizations were focused on the current state of carbon footprint of products and organisations in all areas of the economy; GHG emissions concerning heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems; use of renewable energy sources; optimal use of natural resources. Further objective of the educational scheme development and training course was to support all cooperated universities in their internationalisation process. By implementing the project, all participants achieved enhanced knowledge and experience in quantifying greenhouse gas emissions at the level of a product and organization as well as holistic view of greenhouse gas reduction options at the level of neighbourhoods and cities towards mitigation climate change through green materials, renewable energy, green technologies.
5092a6c5-e5f1-4e1e-b4b6-a7dd2f2af822.projectDescriptionImplementation:
In the project, six transnational project meetings were held, including the opening and closing meetings. Brief overview of the meetings::
•	Kick-off meeting was the opening meeting of the project. It was organized online on 9.12.2021 (because of Covid 19). Project work plan, tasks and responsibilities, evaluation and reports periods were discussed.
•	1st unscheduled virtual project meeting was held on 10.5.2022 in order to present selected lectures on the topic of the project.
•	2st project meeting was transnational project meeting held at the University of Alicante, Spain from 2.11-4.11.2022. The aim of the meeting was to discuss and propose the first training course. 
•	3nd project transnational meeting took place from 25.4.-27.4.2023 at the University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania. The aim of the meeting was to present and discuss the preparation of the second training course. It was periodical meeting in order to monitor and evaluate the project activities. 
•	4th project meeting: This meeting took place from 4.12-6.12.2023 at the Technical University of Kosice (it was not in Ukraine because of the war, as planned in the proposal).
•	Final meeting was the closing meeting  held in lead partner’s country, Slovakia on 28.-29.10.2024.

Concrete outputs of the project are training scheme, educational materials and handbook presenting the knowledge aimed at determining the greenhouse gas emissions and removals on the level of product - building materials and building services; structures and whole building as well as GHG emissions and removals on the level of organization, neighbourhoods and cities. Results and outcomes of the project are available on the project website https://hieducarbon.tuke.sk/.

a0c91e52-b263-4926-a657-50930a04fa56.projectDescriptionBackground:
Hlavnou myšlienkou projektu bolo vytvoriť sériu seminárov pre študentov odborného vzdelávania a prípravy (OVP) na tému prírodných katastrof v dôsledku zmeny klímy a zamerať sa najmä na ochranu pred prívalovými povodňami. Projekt riešil dve priority:
- Životné prostredie a boj proti zmene klímy: Výstupy projektu podporia zvyšovanie povedomia o životnom prostredí a zmene klímy a pomôžu rozvíjať kompetencie učiteľov a študentov OVP v oblasti pochopenia účinkov zmeny klímy na prírodné katastrofy. Počas realizácie projektu boli zorganizované školiace semináre, jeden zameraný na učiteľov OVP a jeden na študentov. Účasť na nich im prispela k rozvoju kompetencií v oblasti environmentálnej.
- Riešenie digitálnej transformácie a príspevok k inováciám vo vzdelávaní a príprave: Projekt podporil digitálnu transformáciu organizácií OVP tým, že účelne využíva digitálne technológie vo vzdelávaní. Konkrétne projekt podporil využívanie inovatívnych digitálnych nástrojov vytvorením aplikácie rozšírenej reality (AR). Vytvorená bola aj príručka pre učiteľov, ktorá im pomôže rozvíjať ich schopnosti pri uplatňovaní STEAM a využívaní AR. Očakáva sa, že používanie týchto podporných materiálov zmení spôsob, akým sa dnes vzdelávanie a príprava praktizuje.
a0c91e52-b263-4926-a657-50930a04fa56.projectDescriptionObjectives:
Realizáciou projektu PROFF dosiahli partneri projektu tieto ciele v podobe aktivít a výstupov:
-	vytvorili sériu 12 seminárov pre študentov odborného vzdelávania a prípravy na tému "Zmena klímy a ochrana pred prírodnými katastrofami",
-	zvýšili povedomie o vplyve zmeny klímy na prírodné katastrofy,
-	zvýšili využívanie prístupu STEAM vo vzdelávaní v oblasti odborného vzdelávania a prípravy,
-	vyškolili učiteľov o tom, ako aplikovať STEAM a používať rozšírenú realitu vo vyučovaní a učení,
-	zorganizovali podujatia pre učiteľov odborného vzdelávania a prípravy a školy s cieľom predstaviť sériu workshopov a získať účastníkov na pilotný beh,
-	pilotne realizovali sériu seminárov s učiteľmi odborného vzdelávania a prípravy v školách odborného vzdelávania a prípravy,
-	zorganizovali tréning pre študentov na tému "Zmena klímy a ochrana pred prívalovými povodňami",
-	pripravili odporúčania pre vzdelávacie orgány na zaradenie seminárov do národných učebných osnov škôl,
-	zabezpečili udržateľnosť a využívanie výstupov projektu, a to prilákaním zainteresovaných strán a informovaním o úspechoch z realizácie pilotných projektov.
a0c91e52-b263-4926-a657-50930a04fa56.projectDescriptionImplementation:
Aktivity projektu boli rozdelené do štyroch pracovných balíkov:
WP1: Manažovanie projektu – Zabezpečovanie riadenia, monitorovania, hodnotenia kvality procesov a šírenia výsledkov počas celého projektu, vrátane nadnárodných stretnutí.
WP2: Využitie STEAM a rozšírenej reality (AR) – Vývoj seminárov pre učiteľov na výučbu o zmene klímy a prírodných katastrofách, aplikácie AR pre ochranu pred povodňami a príručky o využití STEAM a AR vo vzdelávaní. Zorganizované boli aj školenia pre učiteľov na uplatnenie týchto metód.
WP3: Realizácia seminárov v školách – Nábor študentov, pilotovanie seminárov, nadnárodný workshop a zverejnenie úspešných príbehov z pilotných projektov.
WP4: Udržateľnosť a dopad – Odporúčania pre vzdelávacie orgány, kampane na sociálnych médiách pre učiteľov, multiplikačné a online podujatia na zabezpečenie dlhodobého využitia výsledkov, vrátane zapojenia škôl z odľahlých oblastí.
a0c91e52-b263-4926-a657-50930a04fa56.projectDescriptionResults:
Hlavnými výstupmi projektu sú:
-	séria 12 seminárov "Zmena klímy a ochrana pred prírodnými katastrofami" pre študentov odborného vzdelávania a prípravy,
-	aplikácia AR na uľahčenie realizácie seminárov,
-       príručka pre učiteľov "Uplatňovanie metodiky STEAM a využívanie AR na vzdelávanie proti zmene klímy",
-	brožúra s úspešnými príbehmi z pilotnej fázy.
Ďalšie výsledky projektu sú:
-	školenie pre učiteľov na tému "Uplatňovanie metodiky STEAM a využívanie AR v triede",
-       pilotné uplatnenie workshopov a aplikácia AR v školách odborného vzdelávania a prípravy,
-	nadnárodný workshop pre študentov na tému "Zmena klímy a ochrana pred prívalovými povodňami",
-	zaslanie odporúčaní na zaradenie workshopov do školských osnov vzdelávacím inštitúciám a autoritám,
-	zorganizovanie multiplikačných podujatí (konferencie, webové semináre) v každej zúčastnenej krajine.

d78dd130-5b57-4b32-a74d-83eacaf2546a.projectDescriptionBackground:
The UWB and TUKE joined forces 2 years ago. Due to migration events caused by Russia's war aggression in Ukraine, they decided to apply for a grant aimed at providing effective assistance to Ukrainian students and young people migrating to the CZ a SK. The situation in both cities was challenging. Existing students at the universities dealt with, among other things, supporting their relatives in Ukraine, assistance with relocation to safety, and even facing difficult loss situations. Newly arrived young people (high school students, future university applicants) struggled with the necessary adaptation to a new environment, sought support networks, made friends, overcame cultural differences, and at the same time coped with longing for their families and sought support in dealing with emotional and academic challenges. The project also targeted university staff who faced entirely new work challenges in this context.
The project focused on fostering international cooperation among universities to share best practices, establish effective support mechanisms, provide counseling, and combat migration stigma.
d78dd130-5b57-4b32-a74d-83eacaf2546a.projectDescriptionObjectives: Both universities are located in regions with high migrant growth. Both are so-called regional institutions, offering a basic range of fields of study. At the time of application, UWB recorded around 200 students from Ukraine enrolled in bachelor's and follow-up study programs, with a very similar situation at the TUKE. The number of applicants for studies during the academic years 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 ranged in the hundreds. Both schools are open to any assistance; already at the time of application, they offered a variety of activities that emerged spontaneously and were not anchored in the organizational structures.The aim of the project was to create support services to ensure an inclusive environment at universities and to gain a broader perspective on how to better support and communicate with the target group. With the help of students from both universities and local communities, we contributed to the development of skills and the creation of a sustainable, safe, and inclusive environment in higher education. We focused on the use of storytelling, offering opportunities for non-violent forms of education, and acquainting students with the history, present, culture, politics, and other aspects of their "alternative home.
d78dd130-5b57-4b32-a74d-83eacaf2546a.projectDescriptionImplementation:
Especially in the initial period of the Ukrainian crisis, psychological counseling was provided as part of preventive activities (this took place in the form of support groups or crisis interventions).
As part of adaptation activities, the event "A Student for a Week" was organized (high school students tried out the university system for a week, including lectures, and got acquainted with the university environment in more detail), entrance retreats were organized, and activities of the "Weightless Club" were provided, which, in changing student groups, organized communal breakfasts and cooking, movie screenings, lectures or debates, workshops, and collaborated with other student associations and non-profit organizations outside the university (schedule with description in the appendix).
UWB: Educational activities included teaching the basics of Ukrainian for counseling workers and a training course for students (so-called buddies) along with updating the e-learning course including crisis interventions related to the Ukrainian crisis.
TUKE: Buddy training took place, educational and cultural activities were held with new students from Ukraine, and mentoring training for student buddies was regularly conducted.
d78dd130-5b57-4b32-a74d-83eacaf2546a.projectDescriptionResults:
The project was administratively divided into the following key areas, in which individual and specific activities were then implemented:
- Adaptation activities for high school and university students, inclusion
- Pro-inclusive activities for high school and university students
- Prevention and counseling in the field of mental health
- Support for equality
- Education
- Destigmatization of migration
- Consideration for social and cultural values
The specific outputs of these activities are as follows: "University Student for an Exam" event, Weightless Club, Weightless Chronicle, mobilities, mutual support group, introductory concentration for first-year students, Buddy system, language course for counseling workers, online portal, psychological counseling, support groups.
A detailed description of specific activities is provided in the attachment.

results.resultTitle: Adaptation activities for high school and university students, inclusion
results.resultDescription: The aim of the activity was to provide a (re)socialization function consisting in the transfer of knowledge, experience and skills with the aim of resetting the schemes and procedures that await them in the new environment and reducing the negative impacts caused by the current crisis. Emphasis were placed on the cognitive, but also emotional and conative areas. Teaching needs were supplemented with other activities, preventive activities, support for a healthy lifestyle and mental health. Great importance was focused on supporting interest in study and scientific research, passing on knowledge and experience. The target group had the opportunity to familiarize themselves with the background of the university and scientific centers even before and just after entering the university. Both partner organizations offered a safe and stimulating environment in which the educational process takes place, fully supporting the process of developing individual experiences.
results.resultCategory: Direct effect on participants and project partners

results.resultTitle: Educational activities for high school and university students, inclusion
results.resultDescription: The educational activities of the project are focused on teaching the basics of the Ukrainian language for the consulting workers of both partner organizations and on creating and implementing a course intended for the training of university students - buddhists. Both activities were important for better quality and more effective help to young Ukrainians, the emphasis in both courses was on the practical part (i.e. on the ability to use the acquired knowledge purposefully). "First aid" in the field of mental health is based on practical procedures resulting from a certain situation and setting a sense of safety, promoting dignity and respect for the rights of others. Although we all know this, we would like to offer help within the project to those affected by the war aggression of the Russian Federation on the territory of Ukraine. It is essential for support service providers to have at least a basic command of the migrants' language and thereby promote their sense of security.
results.resultCategory: Direct effect on participants and project partners

results.resultDescription: Questions of personal well-being, psychological resistance or vulnerability, coping with workload and stress are often discussed in society recently. There is certainly no need to argue about the need for psychological support services for people affected by the current war crisis. The experiences they brought with them when they ran away from their home are not transferable. After mobilizing the forces to flee, which certainly brought a lot of exhaustion, fear and uncertainty, the refugees will gradually have to deal with other effects on their mental health - they are troubled by the fear of their partners, fathers and other relatives, friends or first loves, in divided families there will be a shift in the balance, with mothers becoming sole breadwinners, adolescents and young men becoming protectors. The goal of the activity is the implementation of preventive and advisory activities, the provision of crisis intervention services, psychologists, psychiatrists and other experts.

cd7bdeff-8ffd-44a8-b81f-4f65c100e681.projectDescriptionBackground: The MicroHUB project was created as a response to the economic and social crisis emphasized by the pandemic COVID-19. Although the crisis has undoubtedly affected all sectors, one of the sectors hit the most has been the craft and the arts. The MicroHUB project, therefore, aims to help artists and crafters to take full advantage of today's technology, and at the same time teach them creative entrepreneurial thinking. It aims to help either existing creative micro-businesses or build new ones to be competitive and efficient in both domestic and foreign markets. At the same time, it helps to reduce unemployment and revitalise the economy both in cities and rural areas.
cd7bdeff-8ffd-44a8-b81f-4f65c100e681.projectDescriptionObjectives:
By developing the digital and entrepreneurial skills and competencies of crafters and artisans the project aimed to foster their capacity to succeed in the labour market and provide them with new opportunities. The MicroHUB project partners wanted to achieve the following objectives:
- To develop entrepreneurial and digital skills of people holding or wanting to create a microenterprise
- to empower teaching staff to be more prepared for the challenges connected with digitalization and provide them with a more up-to-date skillset (project-oriented teaching methods, digital tools etc.)
- to enable people to gain new skills which would enrich their professional life and open new doors for them in the labour market 
- to create a digital platform to provide a space for network creation and product promotion for entrepreneurs from rural areas
cd7bdeff-8ffd-44a8-b81f-4f65c100e681.projectDescriptionImplementation:
A number of activities have been carried out within the project, reaching a large number of stakeholders such as crafters, artisans, artists, policymakers, chambers, associations, NGOs, business support organisations, accelerators, etc., thanks to the partners' extensive network of contacts. The following activities have been implemented:
 
 - PR1 (T1.1): Inception meetings with local and national stakeholders to identify skill gaps in crafters' and artisans´ learning – 78 stakeholders reached
- PR1 (T1.2.): meeting with expert representatives of the selected EU projects presenting the best practices in entrepreneurial education, business creativity thinking, and crafters support projects (at national and international levels) – 20 participants
- PR1 (T1.2.): a questionnaire survey to gain more in-depth knowledge on the areas that need to be supported in crafters´ entrepreneurial education – 121 participants reached
 - PR2 (T2.3): Training material development consisting of 10 MOOC modules
- PR2 (T2.4): Peer review and Testing of the materials during C2 – 13 experts
- PR3 (T3.1, T3.4): Design of innovative multilingual online tool consisting of the MOOC course and open catalogue for matchmaking and subsequent testing of developed materials – MOOC was piloted to 270 participants and 71 crafters uploded their profile into the online catalogue
- PR4 (T4.2): implementation of the Individual online acceleration procedure for entrepreneurs - 35 entrepreneurs
- (C1) 5-day training of 15 entrepreneurs + 8 trainers in Transformative Business Models for creativity micro businesses in Bulgaria 
- (C2) 5-day training of 13 experts in the ‘MicroHUB’ approach: Training of experts in individual acceleration and mentoring in Sweden
cd7bdeff-8ffd-44a8-b81f-4f65c100e681.projectDescriptionResults:
Following resuluts were produced:
- (PR1) Competence Matrix for Digital entrepreneurship and business creative thinking for crafters in rural areas. The Matrix serves as a basis for the whole project and it was created through the process of identification of skills gaps in entrepreneurial learning of crafters and artisans (78 stakeholders), as well as through extensive quantitative (121 participants) and qualitative research (20 experts).  
- (PR2) The Transformative Business Model for creativity micro businesses that consist of 10 MOOC modules. Each module consists of theory and interactive exercises to provide an innovative curriculum to foster digital skills and entrepreneurial thinking of crafters and artisans who either have or wish to establish their own microbusinesses. 
- (PR3) Design of innovative multilingual online tool consisting of two parts: open catalogue for matchmaking which serves as an online space to facilitate international network creation and product promotion of crafters and artisans in (not only) rural areas. 71 crafters and artisans uploaded their profile in total. Innovative online course based on the information provided in the Transformative Business Model was piloted to 270 participants (originally 140 particants were planned). 
 - (PR4) Individual online acceleration procedure for entrepreneurs. Within the Individual online acceleration procedure 2 experts (14 in total)  from each partner country provided services to 5 creative entrepreneurs (35 in total), ending up with tailored business plan creation and mentoring. Together 700 hours of mentoring were provided.

Apart from that, the project consortium created a project website (https://www.facebook.com/microhubproject), social media channel (Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/microhubproject), dissemination materials (leaflets and brochures, newsletters), dissemination reports (every 6 months), quality assurance reports (every 6 months), exploitation strategy, Management and financial plan, progress reports, interim report and final report.

3b710500-1916-4e40-bf3b-351d6358a708.projectDescriptionBackground:
The decision to apply for this project was driven by the recognition that it offers an optimal framework to address shared needs among all participant organizations. The primary goal is to develop transnational cooperation that fosters innovative curricula promoting cross-entrepreneurial mindsets and competences, particularly focusing on digital skills. The project is designed with a pan-European perspective, aiming to be inclusive and introduce a global approach into the curricula. This approach, while addressing local challenges, also tackles common needs at a European level.

The project has served as a platform to collaboratively work on these aspects, providing an opportunity to enrich a new paradigm where Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) engage in strong partnerships to enhance competences in curricula with a European Union transnational approach. The overarching objective is to create a more comprehensive and globally-oriented educational framework.
3b710500-1916-4e40-bf3b-351d6358a708.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The project was structured around three major objectives:
(i) Develop Innovative Curricular Methods: The primary goal was to create innovative curricular methods that foster a cross-domain entrepreneurship mindset in students. This involves addressing challenges in both social and economic domains through collaborative efforts with relevant stakeholders.
(ii) Enlarge Digital Competences: The second objective focused on expanding digital competences. This entailed developing applied skills essential for fostering entrepreneurial activities mentioned earlier. The aim was to ensure that curricular models incorporate these digital competences as a core component.
(iii) Work in a Transnational Environment: The project emphasized working within a transnational environment where participants could learn from each other and share best practices. The objective was to add value to the activities by addressing pan-European challenges and perspectives, enriching and enlarging the overall project results.
3b710500-1916-4e40-bf3b-351d6358a708.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The project aimed to transform transnational cooperation into robust curricular material addressing digital skills and cross-domain entrepreneurial competences in students, preparing them to confront societal challenges. To achieve this, the project built its results through the following activities:
(i) Mapping Digital Skills and Cross-Domain Entrepreneurial Competences: An initial step involved mapping the essential digital skills and cross-domain entrepreneurial competences required for effective student engagement.
(ii) Identifying and Tailoring Curricular Materials: The project identified new curricular materials and adapted existing ones in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) to align with the mapped competences, ensuring relevance and applicability.
(iii) Facilitating Student International Projects: Action learning was facilitated through student international projects, providing a practical platform for mastering competencies in real-world scenarios.
(iv) Local Engagement and Third Mission of Universities: The project extended its impact locally, reaching out to civic society and implementing actions to make universities more entrepreneurial, aligning with the third mission of universities.
(v) Elaborating a Pedagogical and Informative Book: The project culminated in the creation of a pedagogical and informative book. This publication encapsulates the actions undertaken and the results achieved throughout the project, serving as a valuable resource for dissemination and knowledge sharing.
3b710500-1916-4e40-bf3b-351d6358a708.projectDescriptionResults:
The Handbook of Digital Skills and Cross-Domain Entrepreneurial Competences For Societal Challanges stands out as a truly essential and distinctive project result. It serves as a valuable resource for teachers, educators, and trainers worldwide, providing insights into a carefully planned processof getting to know why the learning ecosystems need to adapt and resiliently foresee the competencies bringing us closer to facing societal challenges. Moreover, it supports local groups associated with civic society, offering knowledge on how to effectively address societal challenges through competencies dedicated to the digital society and enriched entrepreneurial mindsets.
Other noteworthy and valuable results of the project include:
(i) Smooth Analysis Tool: An in-depth analysis of digital skills and cross-domain entrepreneurial competences was conducted, accompanied by a tool that enables the smooth mapping of competencies in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs).
(ii) Curricular Materials: The project produced curricular materials designed to help individuals master the identified competencies within HEIs. Additionally, these materials contribute to shaping the mindset of trainers and teachers towards societal challenges.
(iii) Guidance on Peer Learning Techniques: Teachers were provided with guidance on peer learning techniques, enhancing their ability to foster collaborative learning environments.
(iv) Case Studies: Several case studies were developed, showcasing real situations that necessitate the application of skills and competences. The project also presented ideas on how to leverage these case studies for the benefit of learners, trainers, and civic society.
The project's focus on a transnational/global perspective enabled HEIs from multiple countries to engage in peer learning actions. Simultaneously, it created opportunities for seamless dissemination of results within the collaborative environments of HEIs, ensuring strong project sustainability.

results.resultTitle: R1. Mapping interdisciplinary competences and needs - the analysis
results.resultDescription: This results highlights the endeavors made to analyze the requirements and capabilities essential for advancing digital skills and cross-domain entrepreneurship to address societal challenges. Collaborating within an interdisciplinary environment involving multiple academic institutions, our objective was to examine the extent to which the necessary skills and competences are incorporated into courses relevant for addressing societal challenges.
results.resultCategory: Dissemination material

results.resultDescription: This collection of practical educational materials is founded on the identification and pan-European analysis of the most essential skills and competences. During the elaboration process, emphasis was strongly placed on learning within internal, interdisciplinary thematic working groups. The exchange of multidisciplinary and cross-disciplinary experiences enabled the improvement of the curricula. During the evaluation and discussion of the curricular material, which encompasses digital skills and cross-domain entrepreneurial competences for addressing societal challenges, we sought real cases to reveal the depth and specificity of the skills and competences covered. Therefore, the curricula are genuinely cross-disciplinary and multidisciplinary, with modules extending beyond the basic education and training outcomes.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: R3. Guide for the teachers on students' peer learning activities
results.resultDescription: The training programme presented here primarily relies on two outcomes: the needs analysis and curricular material. It facilitates the essential preparations for continuing with the learning and teaching processes. The outlined action ensures a structured approach to preparing and conducting peer learning activities, manifested in the form of an intensive week programme and a one-and-a-half-day guided, interactive workshop inclusive of teaching staff. Furthermore, it can serve as an exemplar (replicative material) for developing other intensive learning, teaching, and training programmes.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: R4. Action learning case studies: from living labs to hackathons
results.resultDescription: A comprehensive analysis of potential local events, aimed at addressing contemporary societal challenges in various regional contexts, formed the foundation for understanding how learners may apply their skills and competences. Volunteers, learners, teachers, researchers, and local organizations actively participated in peer- and facilitated learning sessions to explore effective ways of tackling societal challenges. This material contributes to a deeper understanding of real-case knowledge regarding the competences required and utilized during these events. It takes the form of a testimony, offering practical insights on evaluating the facilitators and barriers associated with the content of action learning.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: R5. Handbook of Digital-skills and cross-domain entrepreneurship for societal challenges
results.resultDescription: The development of competencies related to digital skills and entrepreneurial competences is directly aligned with both the interdisciplinary nature of knowledge domains and the consideration of societal challenges. The handbook practically discusses what should be understood by these societal challenges and how to integrate them into higher education, discussing various examples linked to different social domains. The need to develop capabilities and competencies to address these challenges is evident, particularly when we specifically consider the digital skills and entrepreneurial mindset of learners. The handbook aims to serve as a reference for discussion and assessment of practical cases. It provides readily applicable practical pedagogical material.

cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectTitle: Digital Art Courses in Higher Education Institutions
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectTags: Creating new, innovative or joint curricula or courses|Creativity, arts and culture|Digital skills and competences
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectLevel2Label: Partnerships for cooperation and exchanges of practices
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectDescriptionBackground:
Modern societies are undergoing a rapid digital transformation. We are challenged to cope and succeed in the emerging digital age. This project responds to the needs for digital qualifications and for innovative learning and teaching practices in the higher education sector. There has been a thorough analysis of the needs of the project's target groups - namely art educators, art students and art institutions - in terms of how they can thrive in a digital environment.
Art educators need to be able to keep up with today's digital transformation, which affects all sectors of the economy, including the creative and artistic professions. Their personal digital competencies must be enhanced and their skills in creating innovative digital curricula must be developed. Art students need to be introduced to the concept of digital art and the opportunities and markets this field can offer them in the future. Students represent the next generation of workers and must be able to respond to the changes that digitalisation brings. Higher education institutions in the arts must be able to offer innovative, trans-disciplinary and contemporary programmes to their students.
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The objectives of implementing the project were to:
-Develop Educational and Knowledge Resources for integrating digital art into Art School teaching practices.
-Offer training in innovative digital art and trans-disciplinary approaches for arts academics to enhance curriculum design, delivery, and assessment.
-Enable arts students to acquire digital skills and competencies.
- Increase the visibility of arts institutions, improve their reputation and attract talent and funding by including digital arts courses in their curricula.
-Promote lifelong learning in art schools by offering digital art short courses leading to micro-credentials.
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectDescriptionImplementation:
For Project Result 1, which involves developing a Training Module for art educators on Digital Arts, we conducted a needs assessment, established learning objectives, defined the structure, developed training materials, and conducted evaluations. As a result, 4 training modules were developed, consisting of a total of 54 step-by-step instructional videos.

For Project Result 2, aiming to create a Pedagogical Framework (Curriculum) on Digital Arts, we planned the framework, conducted research, designed content and methods for one core and one elective course, and finally developed materials and tools such as a learners' book, workbook and teachers' guide, as well as other open educational resources.

For Project Result 3, focusing on the development of a curriculum for a short digital arts foundation course leading to micro-credentials, we surveyed stakeholder and designed the course based on the results of the survey, designed the course for micro-credentials and conducted peer review and planned the form of assessment. We investigated the possibility of micro-credentials being issued by universities in partner countries. Due to the lack of clear national regulations, universities do not have an agreed path for granting micro-credentials, but this issue will probably be resolved in the near future, as the need is pressing in all partner countries.

In addition, we managed the progress and quality of the project through various project management activities such as monitoring progress and quality, organising project meetings and arranging dissemination events. We also engaged in dissemination, communication and exploitation activities to ensure that the project results effectively reached the targeted audiences.
cb70c3da-56c3-430e-a7ff-8c951ca36e0a.projectDescriptionResults:
The concrete outputs and results of our project include:
PR1. Training Modules for art educators on Digital Arts.
We have developed four comprehensive training modules to equip art teachers with knowledge, skills and approaches to digital art. The modules are designed to enhance teachers' competencies in integrating digital elements into traditional analogue curricula. In addition, they are designed for the self-learning and upskilling of art students. Each module consists of 10-12 lessons and videos with visualisation of the final results.  All training modules consist of 54 step-by-step instructional videos and are widely available on the Digarted channel on YouTube. The modules cover various aspects of digital art, including artificial intelligence and digital painting, motion graphics, 3D modelling and game art. Playlists cover the following topics:
Module 1 - AI + Digital Painting
1. Artificial Intelligence - Dall E 2
2. Introduction to Digital Painting in Photoshop
3.  Stable Diffusion - generating images
4. Digital painting - character: robot
5. Digital Art Photomontage
6. Animated Picture
7. Halftone - style change
8. Typography poster
9. Gradients and textures 
10. Digital art - finale

Module 2 - Motion Graphic: Adobe Illustrator + Adobe After Effects
1. Introduction - Adobe Illustrator
2. Palette, Library, pencil&brush
3. Art Workshop Poster
4. Character
5. Character - Pose
6. Workshop poster advertisement
7. Introduction - After Effects
8. Animation. Shapes and logos
9. Puppet tool and text and precomposition
10. Tricky, morphing, path animation and graph editor
11. Advertising + sounds

Module 3 - 3d - Blender
1. Intro 3D 
2. AddMesh
3. Asset Browser 
4. Edit Mode 
5. Modeling - pencil & brush
6. Basic materials 
7. Render (camera & light) 
8. UV texture 
9. Physics (rigid body) 
10. Texture and shaders 
11. Sculpture 
12. Animation

Module 4 - Game Art
1. Third person map - introduction to UE5
2,  Materials and lights 
3. Modeling mode 
4. Blender + Unreal Engine 5 (.fbx)
5. Landscape and foliage mode 
6. Ambient sounds and elevators 
7. Animation in Blender and UE5 
8. Trigger and E key Lesson 
9. Messages (Adobe Illustrator, Blender and UE 5)
10. Exporting and packing the game
All videos include automatically generated subtitles in all possible languages.

PR2. Pedagogical Framework (Curriculum) on Digital Arts for one core and one elective digital art course:
We developed a Pedagogical Framework (Curriculum) designed to support teachers in incorporating digital art courses into higher school education art programs. This framework contains syllabus for two courses:  
- The Core course in fundamentals of 2D graphics and multimedia
- The Elective course in fundamentals of 3D graphics
The syllabus includes: Courses description, Prerequisites, Teaching methods, Course content, Final assessment and Expected learning outcomes.
We have developed educational materials to support teachers and students in the process of teaching and learning digital arts:
-	a learners' book, 
-	a workbook 
-	a teachers' guide
All these materials are available for download in pdf format from the project website in 6 languages: English, Polish, Serbian, Greek, Slovak, Latvian.
Other open educational resources, such as presentations and sample lectures, are available in English on the project website.

PR3. Curriculum for a short-duration learning course on the basics of digital art leading to micro-credentials:
We developed a Curriculum for a 3D Design and Motion Graphics Mastery, which in the future will lead to gain the micro-credentials. The Short- Duration Learning Course of 3D Design and Motion Graphics Mastery curriculum contains: Course Overview, Course Content, Micro-credentials Assessments, Course Format, Learning outcome, Evaluation of the student's skills, Evaluation quiz and The course evaluation questionnaire. 

In addition to the above results, the 5th training module was created as part of open educational resources. This module is titled “Interior Design and Artificial Intelligence Course.” It is a basis for teachers conducting interior design classes using digital tools, and for students to self-study in order to improve their competences. Furthermore, it can serve as background material for courses leading to micro -credentials. It contains 5 video lessons. It is available on the Digarted YouTube channel.

a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectTitle: Network for Inter-Institutional Cooperation in Entrepreneurial Education
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectTags: International cooperation, international relations, development cooperation|Entrepreneurial learning - entrepreneurship education|ICT - new technologies - digital competences
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectDescriptionBackground:
NICE - Network for Inter-Institutional Cooperation in Entrepreneurial Education was a project created to support school education through activities supporting entrepreneurial competencies (ECo) among secondary school students.
ECo is understood as an ability to use opportunities and ideas and transform them into values for others. The core of ECo is creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, initiative, persistence, ability to cooperate toward planning and managing projects with cultural, social, or commercial value. Business skills are based on creativity containing imagination, strategic thinking, problem-solving, and critical constructive reflection in the frame of developing creative processes and innovations. It is required to have skills both to work individually and in teams, to mobilize resources (human/staff), and to persist in performing the activity. 
The key area is to support the skills mentioned above and this is where the partners of the project (universities from 4 different countries) aim their activities. Although the universities work with university students, thanks to the cooperation with secondary schools and this project, they can work with and influence secondary school students and teachers.
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The objectives of the project mainly are:
• Promoted entrepreneurship,
• Provided secondary students with knowledge of soft and hard skills, that will help them to develop their entrepreneurial competencies,
• Developed a manual on available online tools and their use,
• Facilitated the creation of a cooperating network from secondary schools and universities in the participating countries,
• Facilitated networking and sharing of knowledge, experiences and best practices,
• Created a platform to promote entrepreneurship education through a three-part competition and several different scenarios. 
• Promoted digital competencies and their use among secondary school students and secondary school teachers.
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectDescriptionImplementation:
Activities that have been realized within the project:
• Development and pilot testing of lectures in economic sciences (finance, management, accounting, marketing, business economics).
• Development and pilot testing of national and international competitions with entrepreneurial topics for secondary school students (organized 4 national competitions and 1 international competition)
• Creation of a manual with an overview of selected online tools that can be used in creating a competition or in teaching 
• Creating short videos to supplement the online tools manual.
• Organization of dissemination events in each country and participation in other events where the NICE project was promoted.
a2175870-2e85-4740-92d1-1cd8760284bd.projectDescriptionResults:
The objectives of the project will be achieved through the development of the following intellectual outputs:
1. NICE IO1: NICE Library of educational lectures and practical tasks (1 Report from survey, 83 lectures, pilot testing 1650+ students)
2. NICE IO2: Creation of competition in the area of entrepreneurial development (5 manual - Rules of competition in each language, 1 manual - Rules of international competition, 1 set of Practical tasks for competition, which can be used in lectures too)
3. NICE IO3: Portfolio of online tools usable for the organization of international competition (1 Online tools manual, 1 manual about Artificial intelligence, and 9 short videos about selected online tools).

171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectTitle: Promoting Sustainability as a Fundamental Driver in Software Development Training and Education
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectTags: ICT - new technologies - digital competences|Environment and climate change|Social responsibility of educational institutions
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectDescriptionBackground: Currently, sustainable practices in the context of software engineering are not taught at Computer Science courses. However, the current amount of electricity spent by servers on running programs is far from being trivial. Therefore, software engineers need to take into account more sustainable choices, for instance, a programming language or data structure that will require less energy. The proponents of this project felt the need to educate software engineers to consider sustainability in all aspects of the software engineering process. This project targets university students from computer science courses that could bring these practices to their professional lives in the near future and change the way software companies perceive the impact of running software on the environment.
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectDescriptionObjectives: We aim to provide future software engineers with essential skills to develop software that is not only functionally correct, but also easy to maintain and evolve, that is durable, has a low impact and uses the hardware it is running on in the most energy-efficient way.
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectDescriptionImplementation: Two summer schools and two dissemination events were implemented with the goal of promoting good sustainability practices in the software engineering process.  Two teacher training activities were also implemented with the goal of preparing material for the two summer schools among the teachers and to discuss pedagogical methods and goals.
171462f8-f59f-44a0-a3e4-03b48d4f249b.projectDescriptionResults: Within this project, two teacher training activities, two summer schools and two dissemination activities were organized. Moreover, several scientific publications were released, the proceedings of the teacher training events are publicly available and the proceedings of the two summer schools are being published at LNCS Springer.

afc47e6a-c710-47c1-9d5f-3e9a62693968.projectDescriptionBackground:
The most wanted professionals today did not exist ten years ago. 

In 10 years, robots will do 65% of the work we do today. EC Industrial Policy Strategy brings together all existing and new horizontal and sector-specific initiatives into a comprehensive industrial strategy that will empower industry to create jobs, boost Europe's competitiveness, foster investment and innovation in clean and digital technologies and defend Europe’s regions and workers most affected by industrial change. The Strategy provisions unlocking the potential of Key Enabling Technologies. A rigorous need analysis of the EC, underpinning the Industrial Policy Strategy, combined with the huge theoretical and practical expertise of the project team in robotics and education, lead to the current project. 

In the Bulgarian context, the project contributes to the activities of the Ministry of Education and Science targeting the modernization of the educational system with view of providing accessible and high - quality education by improving the technical infrastructure and equipment at schools, as well as training the teachers to utilize it. It is in line with the National Development Program BG2020, and with Europe 2020 goals for smart growth in EU.
afc47e6a-c710-47c1-9d5f-3e9a62693968.projectDescriptionObjectives:
Vocational Education and training and technical universities face the challenge to provide KETs knowledge and expertise to the new generation. Robotics is an integral part of the KET with most the important share in the growth of the European industries (Euro Stat). Robotics education is still seen as an extra-curricular activity and a part of informal education. Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science reported 393 extra-class clubs on robotics with more than 6000 pupils in 2017/2018 school year in Bulgaria. Efforts must be devoted not only to the development of robotic hardware and software for education but also to the design of learning material and appropriate curriculum and to the role of the teacher.

A pre-project survey identified the main obstacles to robotics education according to the experts from the participating organizations - universities, VET and secondary schools, and NGOs. Vast majority of the respondents identified the expensive equipment as the main reason for avoiding robots in schools (91%), followed by lack of open educational resources and ready to use curricula (78%), and lack of staff support and understanding (56%).
afc47e6a-c710-47c1-9d5f-3e9a62693968.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The main objective of the project team was to contribute to the enhancement of the open, innovative education on KETs in the partnering countries and the region. Additionally, it aimed to foster social inclusion and to provide learning opportunities to VET students from schools with insufficient availability of equipment, thus providing equal access to the educational content to all students. Additionally, in times of crisis, lock-down and physical distancing, the network of Virtual Robo Labs provides innovative, sustainable environment for distance learning, collaboration, and knowledge exchange for the VET students and teachers in Robotics in EU. 

The project team developed six intellectual outputs and trained more than 20 trainers to utilize them in Train-the-trainer Knowledge Exchange LTT activity. The results were show-cased in all partner countries to more than 400 participants in three multiplier events - part of the Robo Olympics international live competition between the NITRO Robo Clubs from Bulgaria, Romania and Slovakia. 

Four transnational project meetings contributed to the synergies in the team - leading to ongoing cooperation, co-creating and knowledge exchange, as well as progress tracking and risk-monitoring.
afc47e6a-c710-47c1-9d5f-3e9a62693968.projectDescriptionResults: To address the needs and to overcome the highest obstacle, the project team created a Virtual Robo Lab - a robotic simulator that provides the students with full immersive experience of a real Robo Lab. While the curricula-gap was identified before the survey and addressed accordingly as described above, the lack of support was unexpected. To address this need, the project team created a Teachers' Toolkit with lessons and guidelines how to create a IT Robo Clubs and join the Network of IT Robo Clubs. A platform for IT Robo Games was created and published. New local Robo Clubs were created in all partner countries. The team piloted an international online Robo Olympics using features of the IT Robo Games platform.

669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectTitle: Benchmarking for Quality Assurance in e-learning provision of VET education
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectTags: Quality Improvement Institutions and/or methods (incl. school development)|ICT - new technologies - digital competences|Quality Assurance
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectDescriptionBackground: The project answered the urgent needs coming with COVID-19 - to assure high-quality online education. The pandemic caused the largest disruption to education systems in history, affecting nearly 1.6 billion students in more than 190 countries. The need to modernize and digitally transform education has become increasingly urgent at that time. In Slovakia, Greece, Italy and Spain very few schools were prepared for online education and there were no generally accepted criteria or requirements for e-learning. Some VET institutions developed their own criteria to ensure the quality of e-learning, but most VET organizations did not have guidelines.  VET schools have started developing e-learning opportunities, but still without following a quality framework or national guidelines. The need to respond promptly to learners due to the disruption of classes has led to the recognition and use of distance learning as largely homologous. Many schools had already made great efforts to digitize before the Covid19, but the pandemic turned a significant part of teaching towards e-learning. Therefore, to ensure a high-quality transition to e-learning, quality monitoring, and the related benchmarking project have become very relevant and necessary.
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The project aims to contribute to building digital education readiness and to mitigating the impact of the COVID-19 crisis. By implementing the BEQUEL project, the project partners wanted to achieve the following objectives:
1. To examine the existing approaches for quality in digital e-learning and pedagogies in VET at the European level.
2. To develop a quality assurance framework and self-assessment questionnaires for quality assurance in e-learning provision for VET organizations.
3. To develop a thematic portal on quality assurance in digital transformation with various content, documents, links, articles, and videos.
4. To develop an online benchmarking tool for quality assurance in e-learning for VET providers.
5. To create and mobilize a Community of Practice of VET providers across the EU through social media.
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectDescriptionImplementation:
During the project life, the consortium implemented the following activities:
Development activities (A) related to the Intellectual Outputs (IO):
IO1: “Benchmarking methodology and tools” activities: A1 State of Play; A2 Quality assurance framework for e-learning practices for VET schools and organisations; A3 Benchmarking methodology; A4 Benchmarking questionnaire for VET providers; A5 Validation of benchmarking questionnaire; A6 Translation of benchmarking questionnaires.
IO2: “Online benchmarking tools”: A1 Technical implementation of English version and integration; A2 Internal testing of English version; A3 Development of national versions; A4 Internal testing of national versions; A5 Collection of benchmarking data; A6 Launching of the online benchmarking tools; A7 Development of videos.
• Project management activities 
• Dissemination and exploitation activities
• Quality assurance and evaluation activities
• Learning, Teaching, and Training Activity
• Organised 14 virtual meetings
• Organised the kick-off meeting and three transnational project meetings in a hybrid format
•  Multiplier Events
669deced-e2f6-4324-b45a-b81f48736625.projectDescriptionResults:
The project developed two main outputs: 
• IO 1: Benchmarking methodology and tools to ensure quality in e-learning procedures of VET organizations.  A quality assurance framework for e-learning procedures was developed as part of this output, forming the basis for developing a self-assessment questionnaire for VET organizations. In addition, this output contains a benchmarking methodology aimed at comparing the quality procedures in the provision of e-learning in VET with the procedures of similar organizations in the same country and also in comparison with Europe using an algorithm based on evaluating quality criteria on a five-point scale. 
• IO 2: Online benchmarking tools. This output is based on the benchmarking methodology and the online self-assessment questionnaire, which was created as part of IO1 and hosted on the "BEQUAL and BEQUEL" platform (www.begual.info). The development of the online benchmarking tool was heavily dependent on a promotional campaign that engaged users and obtained a sufficient number of completed questionnaires necessary for benchmarking with organizations in the same country and also across Europe.

and internships in Higher Education in partners’ countries, results from interviews and surveys
with students, companies, and HEI staff regarding required characteristics of internship
programs, entrepreneurial competencies to be developed, and gamification. It concludes
with specific recommendations for the internship model for the acquisition of entrepreneurial
skills and on the entrepreneurial competencies grid to be adapted. This study intended to serve as a basis for the development of common ground among the
partnership and to provide direction to the Enter.Mode process towards an entrepreneurial internship model.
The background study was elaborated through a combination of desk research, interviews, and surveys.

results.resultDescription:
The mentor’s guide is the main tool for the implementation of the EnterMode model, during the EnterMode internships, since it offers practical guidelines and tools. The EnterMode internship models’ aim is to promote the acquisition of entrepreneurial skills and competences by students in higher education during their internships. It is constituted of several phases, which combine different elements that lead to the development of the entrepreneurial skills. For each phase, the mentors’ guide offers a set of step-by-step instructions and suggestions to enhance the internship programme and implement the EnterMode model.
The guide is addressed to the different actors that take part in the EnterMode internships, namely HEI administration officers, HEI academic tutors and company mentors.

results.resultDescription: Serious games are the games that are designed for a primary purpose other than pure entertainment. They use traditional game techniques around serious business concepts.  The goal of the ENTER.MODE serious game is to help players to develop 6 entrepreneurial competences by completing several tasks (minigames). The players’ main goal is to have a successful job interview with the Τop Manager at the end of the game. This can only be achieved if they complete all the required tasks (minigames) with a high enough total score and collect the badges the game offers -the highest the level of the badge, the better.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: Train The Trainer program - selection documents
results.resultDescription:
The selection process to select trainers for the new center followed a three-stage procedure: 
- First, the content of the selection process was prepared. That is, the application form and the interview schedule were prepared.  
- Then the program was advertised and interested academic staff applied for the training. Based on the application form the Indian partners selected staff with training potential and invited them to attend an interview. 
- Finally, the selection of staff that would be part of the program was the base of the interview procedure that was conducted by the EU partners.

4e136247-ecf9-4440-9b1d-5ec0db857a4c.projectDescriptionBackground:
The DigitalSoftSkills@Ulysseus (D2S@Ulysseus) project was carried out by the European alliance Ulysseus (Université Côte d’Azur, France; University of Seville, Spain; University of Genoa, Italy; Technical University of Košice, Slovakia; MCI | The Entrepreneurial School®, Austria; Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences, Finland) to modernize education in Europe by improving the digital skills of educators and adapting pedagogies to meet the demands of an increasingly digital world. 
The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the need to rethink education and training systems to adapt to the digital age and exposed the gaps that need to be addressed for effective digital education. Digital technologies have been widely used to ensure continuity of learning, teaching, and assessment, but this has highlighted the need to improve teachers' digital pedagogical skills in terms of student engagement and inclusivity. Learners also need to develop the necessary skills to effectively use digital learning systems.
According to the OECD's 2018 study (TALIS), less than 40% of educators felt prepared to use digital technologies in teaching, and online learning resources and content need to be more relevant, interactive, and user-friendly. Therefore, as announced by the 2020 open public consultation on the Action Plan for Digital Education, it is necessary to improve digital and transversal skills to ensure that everyone in Europe can live, work, and thrive in the digital age. To support the EU's digital transformation strategy, education and training institutions must adopt digital technologies through systemic organizational change.
The European alliance Ulysseus is fully committed to the digital transformation of education through the development of a European virtual campus. The D2S@Ulysseus project aims to address the gaps in digital education by modernizing it and improving the digital skills of educators, ensuring that all learners can actively participate in inclusive and high-quality digital education.
4e136247-ecf9-4440-9b1d-5ec0db857a4c.projectDescriptionObjectives:
The DigitalSoftSkills@Ulysseus (D2S@Ulysseus) project, proposed by the Ulysseus alliance, aims to support higher education institutions in preparing for global digital transformation. Its goal is to harness the potential of digital technologies for learning and teaching.
The main target groups of D2S@Ulysseus include:
•	Academic staff members.
•	Students, including those with specific needs.
•	Partner institutions and their ecosystem.
To enhance the effectiveness of digital education and training, the project focuses on key actions:
•	Developing Digital Soft Skills for teachers and students.
•	Encouraging collaboration and sharing of best practices in Digital Soft Skills and innovative teaching methods.
•	Creating a more engaging and inclusive evaluation and recognition system through digital badges (Open Badges). 
•	Enhancing the visibility of digital skills by strengthening recognition of Open Badges and creating a specific ecosystem for digital skills passports.
These main objectives will be strengthened by the creation of joint international catalogues of digital skills for teachers and students, as well as two main guidelines: digital education guidelines and Digital Soft Skills guidelines.
In summary, the following results are expected:
•	International Joint Digital Soft Skills Catalogue for teachers
•	Survey to identify teachers’ Digital Soft skills needs
•	Online teachers’ self-assessment tool
•	Digital Education Guidelines
•	Syllabus and contents of 1 introductory MOOC on Digital Soft Skills for education
•	Syllabus and contents of 5 courses on Digital Soft Skills for teachers
•	International Joint Soft Digital Soft Skills Catalogue for students 
•	Survey to identify the most relevant Digital Soft Skills for a better student employability
•	Online student self-assessment tool
•	Digital Soft Skills Guidelines
•	Syllabus and contents of 1 introductory MOOC on Digital Soft Skills for better student employability
•	Syllabus and contents of 5 courses on Digital Soft skills for students
•	Survey to evaluate the courses 
•	Ulysseus Digital Soft Skills passports leading to the creation of Open Badges
•	Shared model and awarding criteria for badges
•	Shared guidelines for future expansion of the badges system
4e136247-ecf9-4440-9b1d-5ec0db857a4c.projectDescriptionImplementation:
The D2S@Ulysseus consortium has implemented several activities:
• Intellectual outputs:
IO1: FOSTERING A PERFORMING DIGITAL EDUCATION ECOSYSTEM
o Joint international catalogue of Digital Soft Skills for teachers
o Survey to identify the Digital Soft Skills needs of teachers
o Online self-assessment tool for teachers
o Guidelines for digital education
o Program and content of an introductory MOOC on Digital Soft Skills for education
o Program and content of 5 courses on Digital Soft Skills for teachers
o Survey to evaluate the courses
IO2: IMPROVING STUDENTS' DIGITAL SOFT SKILLS
o Joint international catalogue of Digital Soft Skills for students
o Survey to identify the most relevant Digital Soft Skills for better employability of students
o Online self-assessment tool for students
o Guidelines for Digital Soft Skills
o Program and content of an introductory MOOC on Digital Soft Skills for better employability of students
o Program and content of 5 courses on Digital Soft Skills for students
o Survey to evaluate the courses 
IO3: CREATING "ULYSSEUS DIGITAL SOFT SKILLS PASSPORTS"
o Ulysseus Digital Soft Skills passports leading to the creation of Open Badges 
o Shared model and criteria for awarding Open Badges
o Shared guidelines for future expansion of the Open Badges system
• Transnational meetings: one launch meeting and 4 other transnational meetings were organized for partners to exchange on the project's progress and follow-up.
• Multiplier events: 2 events were organized to communicate project results with academic staff, institutional and business representatives, students, and the public.
To ensure the successful implementation of the project, the appropriate development of intellectual outputs, and the development of a sustainable impact and exploitation of the results, several project management activities were put in place. As the coordinator, Université Côte d’Azur ensured the overall administrative management of the project, including budget control and reporting. Partners coordinated within their own institutions and collaborated on the development and implementation of project activities. An external evaluator contributed to the quality monitoring of the project and the analysis of results and intellectual outputs.
Specifically, project management referred to the following activities:
• Administrative activities for project preparation and progress monitoring.
• Coordination and communication processes among partners (Project Management Committee, online communication, meetings).
• Definition of plans and reports (project management, quality assurance and evaluation, dissemination, sustainability, and exploitation strategy).
• Preparation of financial and activity reports.
4e136247-ecf9-4440-9b1d-5ec0db857a4c.projectDescriptionResults:
The D2S@Ulysseus project achieved the following intellectual results over a period of 24 months:
•	IO1: Foster a high-performing digital education ecosystem - which aims to improve educators' digital pedagogical skills to provide high-quality and inclusive digital education for all learners.
•	IO2: Enhance students' Digital Soft Skills - by developing cross-cutting skills that provide competitive advantages to students entering the job market.
•	IO3: Create "Ulysseus Digital Soft Skills Passports" - enabling online course participants to translate their learning experiences into skills and highlight these skills in the job market.
The project's results and activities have an impact at the local, national, European, and international levels. By improving students' digital skills and educators' digital pedagogical skills, this project addresses the third national priority: the development of cross-cutting and key skills. It also supports the European agenda of developing high-quality and inclusive education and training for learners.
The project's actions benefit the following target groups: teachers, students, partner institutions of the Ulysseus European Alliance, and indirectly their ecosystem, as well as all actors in higher education at the European and international levels.
Thanks to the project's results, teachers and educators acquire new skills and knowledge about distance learning pedagogical tools. This improves their adaptability to digital environments, enables them to assess their students' learning pace, and creates solutions that motivate and engage them. The more effective use of digital technologies by teachers thus facilitates medium-term more personalized, flexible, and student-centred learning.
By strengthening students' digital skills and competencies, the project equips them with the necessary skills to prepare for their future and support their employability upon entering the job market. This action benefits not only students but also the entire ecosystem of partner institutions, as students' skills better meet the needs of the job market.
The higher education institutions of the Ulysseus European University Alliance also benefit from the D2S@Ulysseus project by improving their capacities, expanding their course catalogues, sharing best practices, and promoting cooperation opportunities. The consortium disseminates in the long term the project's results to its respective local ecosystems and international networks.

118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectTitle: A digital tool development to train women from rural areas on literacies
118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectTags: Agriculture, forestry and fisheries|ICT - new technologies - digital competences|New innovative curricula/educational methods/development of training courses
118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectLevel2Label: Cooperation for innovation and the exchange of good practices
