118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectDescriptionBackground:
The project emerged after an analysis of the situation of women in rural areas. During the needs analysis, we identified that women are more likely to be unemployed than men despite of representing over a 45% of the economically working population. Especially in rural areas, their involvement in the labor market and overall participation lagged behind men, facing cultural and educational disadvantages.

Without the correct instruments and tools, VET educators and overall facilitators would oversee the needs from them, not being able to provide a correct guidance and education. 

Educated women can play a bigger role in the development of rural communities, enhance their possibilities and help breaking the barieers that historically kept them discriminated.
118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectDescriptionObjectives:
With the project DigiWomen, we aimed for international cooperation among the five consortium institutions, from different nature and with different strenghts, to address the above mentioned need.

On the one hand, we wanted to address VET trainers and facilitators as the main actors in the education and channelers of the knowledge developed throughout the project. With this aim, we wanted to firstly put into context and value the need to change the current situation and introduce the literacies relevant for the education of women coming from rural areas.

On the other hand, we wanted to address the ultimate beneficiaries from the action, women coming from rural areas. They would have an access to modern education tools with the e-learning platform developed and the relevant curricula on the different literacies covered by the VET curricula from the DigiWomen project.
118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectDescriptionImplementation: The activities from the project were varied. Among the activities we can highlight: Research, information gathering via questionnaire, the development of a handbook for managing the project, the development of an English language-financial-digital-farming literacies handbook, the best-practices cases gathering and research, the development of a VET curricula on English language-financial-digital-farming literacies, the pilot testing of the VET developed curricula, the creation of an e-learning platform, the creation of the e-learning platform manual, creation of guideliness for the e-learning platform, the creation of a project visual identity, the creation of different communciation channels for the project, the implementation of project monitoring meetings, the creation of five multiplier events, the implementation of two transnational project meetings, the constant updating of the different social platforms, the presentation of the project in offline and online events, and more.
118fb731-7d6a-4895-ae3c-cd4457c8cacd.projectDescriptionResults:
We developed a total of four outputs:

- IO1, DIGIWOMEN PROJECT MANAGEMENT HANDBOOK. It included (among others) a detailed work breakdown structure, a communication and dissemination plan, a back-up plan, a financial management plan, evaluation and quality assurance plan, sustainability plan and a Gantt chart.

- IO2. Financial – Digital – Agricultural – English language Literacies Development Handbook. Consisted of a handbook to introduce the literacies covered by the project in a simple, appealing manner for the stakeholders addressed by the project DigiWomen. It included a literature review and a organisation of best practices prepared and organised to showcase the success on similar initiatives.

- IO3. Financial, Digital, Agricultural and English language Literacies VET Curriculum. The curriculum contain the background of the literacies of the project, with deffinitions and approaches to the digital system; used by both VET trainers and women from rural areas.

- IO4. E-learning Platform Construction. An free, open, online platform that included the content developed during IO3 in a digital manner, together with guideliness and a manual for use presented to the future users of the platform.

b9edc0ef-3599-49b2-890d-7076b319f6bb.projectDescriptionBackground: RE-ACT is built on a multi-stakeholders’ approach that brings key players of the quadruple helix into a collaborative hands-on atmosphere leveraged by HEINNOVATE for RIS3. Participating in capacity-building actions and being engaged in the processes of self-reflection and joint negotiation, HEIs, public, private sectors and NGOs will embark into a journey that will strengthen their links and engagement in the regional innovation ecosystem.
b9edc0ef-3599-49b2-890d-7076b319f6bb.projectDescriptionObjectives: RE-ACT- Self-reflection tools for smart universities acting regionally – aims at encouraging Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in becoming more engaged in regional innovation policies and RIS3 (Research and Innovation Strategies for Smart Specialisation), supporting them to rethink and reposition their strategies, structures and actions and establishing links among actors of the quadruple helix. RE-ACT has developed a self-reflection tool – SUNAR - and support resources.
b9edc0ef-3599-49b2-890d-7076b319f6bb.projectDescriptionImplementation: Research activities to understand the potential of HEIs to participate in RIS3 and to decide the best approach to enable HEInnovate to address the regional perspective;The design and launch a self-assessment tool based on HEInnovate;Training courses targeted to HEIs;Training courses targeted to other actors of the quadruple helix;Meetings and events gathering both parties;Training courses targeted quadruple-helix actors from different regions to mainstream RE-ACT resources and methodology.

results.resultTitle: O9: Prodotto innovativo in un nuovo percorso digitale
results.resultDescription:
The University of Calabria presented the Itaca Protocol in the PAES project.
The ITACA Protocol is a certification system based on a multi-criteria analysis that makes it possible to assess the various aspects that define the environmental sustainability of a building by classifying it through the attribution of a performance score.
The protocol is loaded on the PAES platform
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultTitle: O2: Creazione della Piattaforma e-learning per lo SCORM (sharable content object reference model) Modello di Riferimento per gli Oggetti di Contenuto Condivisibile
results.resultDescription: The Italian-Greek Chamber of Commerce was responsible for collecting and processing information on companies operating in the areas of the partnership, operating a sort of screening of companies and distinguishing, on the basis of agreed requirements, those that can be defined as sustainable. In this activity it has been supported by Unical. The activity that the Chamber of Commerce has carried out is the definition of parameters, and possibly indicators, that allow to evaluate and measure the level of sustainability of companies and on the basis of which to structure ad hoc questionnaires to be administered to companies dealing with construction and building materials. The final objective was to create synoptic tables, or a summary document, highlighting the characteristics, initiatives and sustainable activities of the companies registered with the Chamber of Commerce.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultTitle: O10: Metodi per la valutazione degli impatti del progetto e gestione delle criticità
results.resultDescription:
a) Periodic questionnaire. The first questionnaire was administered one year after the start of the project, followed by 3-monthly intervals. It aims to acquire the opinion of the partners on the management methods, on the implementation of the objectives, any problems and criticalities encountered. It will be the instrument to calibrate the work of Unical as the lead institution. 
b) End of meeting questionnaire. At the end of each technical meeting of the project, the partners were given the opportunity to evaluate the effectiveness of the meeting, the interest and clarity of the contents and any suggestions regarding the issues exposed. 
c) Questionnaire on the technical part.  Administered at the end of the training days.

results.resultTitle: IO1 - Entrepreneurial Attitude at University level - Study
results.resultDescription:
The main aim of this IO is to clearly assess strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats of the target groups in the selected countries considering the theme of the project, i.e. knowledge-based entrepreneurship.
Researchers, students, university technical staff, potential entrepreneurs will be invited to provide their views of their training needs. Based upon a common analysis framework, each participating country will analyse their needs, which will be aggregated into a single report, providing relevant recommendations and conclusions for further work.
TheBased on the preliminary analysis of training needs, the consortium has identified a set of contents and tools to address those needs and it intends to have a preliminary feedback from the final beneficiaries as for the relevance of the approach proposed.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

Zidentyfikowano już szereg tematów: przywództwo, podejmowanie ryzyka, marketing, finansowanie początkowe i planowanie biznesowe.

results.resultTitle: IO2 - Recreate workshops programme - Start-up funding - England_EN
results.resultDescription: The aim of IO2 was to develop training materials for the target groups to benefit from in order to meet the training needs of the target groups, as described in the Entrepreneurial attitude Study (O1), include country-specific information, such as legislation, particular procedures, statistical data and more, developed new content to enhance transversal competences for entrepreneurship. Each module was developed as a programme for a workshop, each focused on one specific theme. The final outcome was a modular training course to be implemented with a set of workshops. A series of topics have been already identified: leadership, risk-taking, marketing, start-up funding and business planning.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription: The main objective of this Good Practices Guide is to engage more Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) into designing, implementing and monitoring profitable apprenticeship practices which can benefit the organisation, the apprentice and the entire society. We believe that this Guide will shed light to the benefits, including social benefits, that could derive through the involvement with apprenticeship schemes, while our general goal is to promote Work Based Learning (WBL) in all its forms.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription: Learning Methodology and its executive summaries in all 6 languages have been based on a focused user-oriented approach respecting main innovative research principles: 1. to customize the training process, allowing learning to be adapted to the emergent opportunities, characteristics and interests of each individual, so that the learner himself become the manager of the learning process, thanks to a modular structure of the training tools; 2. to enrich the training program with any valuable contribution from the single Partners; 3. to promote the ability to apply the proposed contents, so that learners involved in the training process can achieve immediate results in their practice; 3. to carry out a critical analysis to respond to emerging needs. It included also the results of the preliminary mapping of the existing knowledge in the project fields (articles, existing learning contents, scientific studies, economic and social analysis.

results.resultTitle: O3 - AuToMa Resources and Learning Integrated Area
results.resultDescription:
The aim of this output has been to design and implement the innovative ICT collaborative solution “AuToMa Resources and Learning Integrated Area”. In detail, Partners identified the best open ICT solutions for learning, knowledge sharing, communication and participation goals, integrating them in a unique easy online solution. Partners designed and adapted this solution on project target groups by an initial testing and next validation of contents. A mix of specialized open source softwares have been identified and customized to provide structure and means
to collaborate, exchange ideas, transfer multimedia contents and coordinate activities. They allowed Partners staff and target groups to create, organize, archive and use an integrated learning system in 6 languages. The knowledge exchange section is available on the following link: http://www.kria.piap.pl/ - Instead the multilanguage e-learning section is available on the following link: http://www.automa-course.piap.pl/en/

results.resultDescription:

The contents have been developed taking in account the previous O1 “AuToMa learning methodology” and O2 “AuToMa guidelines for the learning outputs” developed and adopted to make proper shape of the system functionality, preliminar content adaptation and monitoring of the participation activities.

results.resultTitle: O1-Introduction to IoT technologies and applications
results.resultDescription: The book, targeted for beginners (for example, high school and first year university students or non-technical people), consists of 4 modules. The first module introduces and provides an overview of the main concepts and technologies related to the Internet of Things (IoT): definitions, terminology, hardware and software technologies currently in use.  The second module provides a summary of the electronics concepts necessary for the development of an IoT solution: basic circuitry is presented together with an application chapter. The third module introduces to the reader the Raspberry Pi (the workhorse of IoT) together with several software technologies. The last module showcases the Arduino, sensor based applications (like reading the temperature or the light intensity and more advances hardware applications.

results.resultDescription: The second book, targeted for advanced students, consists of 5 modules. The first module revises the basics of the IoT technologies, followed by four modules that contain more advanced topics. The second module goes in depth into the capabilities of Raspberry Pi and Arduino. We discuss several ways of controlling the Arduino from the Raspberry Pi. The third module relates to the communication protocols between embedded devices. We focus on some of the most used IoT protocols such as: HTTP, MQQT and XMPP. Then, in the fourth module, we present the most popular communication protocols between wired and wireless peripherals and embedded devices: I2C, SPI, BLE and LoRa. In the final output, we have integrated the chapters resulting from O6, O7 and O8. The main result may be received as a book that covers both general aspects of the Internet of Things, but also presents concrete examples where IoT has a great impact: security, power management, and smart cities.

results.resultDescription: This output consists of 21 pages describing how the materials developed under O1, O2, O3, O6, O7 and O8 can be extended and included in the teaching curriculum. The teaching methodology addresses several groups of students: High-School; First-Year University Non-Computer Science Students, First-Year Computer Science University Students (or any other students that have programming knowledge), Advanced University Students. For each category we suggest the book chapters, course slides, laboratory and practical exercises that should be followed for a 12-week course. Moreover, the methodology clearly states the objectives targeted by each component of the intellectual outputs in respect to what knowledge and skills should the students acquire.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription: The web platform developed aggregates all the teaching materials developed in the project. In this way, teachers and students can easily access the IoT knowledge results. The platform is free and open source, meaning that anybody can adapt it and run it on their premises. Currently, the website is hosted in the infrastructure of the University Politehnica of Bucharest and can be accessed at http://seeiot.cs.pub.ro. Anybody can upload, access or download materials. While the files can be downloaded directly by accessing the platform, in order to upload or comment on the existing files, users need to create an account. The educational materials are divided into 3 categories: books, slides and practical exercises which are grouped under each course. To bring the community and gamification aspect to the platform, users can rate and give comments in existing courses.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: O6-EN-Advanced IoT applications: power management topics
results.resultDescription: This output consists of a 50 pages module divided into 3 chapters dealing with the issues and the solutions regarding power management in IoT systems. The chapter dedicated to Advanced IoT applications: power management topics (O6) presents available solutions for energy and power management of IoT technologies. The created content presents procedures to reduce consumption during designing phase for hardware and software. It presents how those solutions affects battery life, compares the popular Raspberry Pi vs. Arduino, deals with various software designs – like polling, interrupts, clock frequency reducing, etc. Various schemes and source codes are presented for a better understanding of the topic and practical implementations of the presented power management for advanced IoT applications are exemplified.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultTitle: O7-EN-1-Advanced IoT applications: smart cities topics
results.resultDescription: This output consists of a 50 pages module divided into 2 chapters dealing with practical applications in the IoT field, with an accent on smart cities solutions. While the first chapter, more theoretical, presents the basic aspects to be taken into account when building commercial and industrial IoT solutions, the second part of the module presents the characteristics of smart city systems. These systems are presented from several points of view: transportation, lighting, and security. The purpose of this module is to give readers an insight on building large-scale, industrial systems. Here, 23 working days belonging to the O7 work load have been transferred from Wyliodrin to the University Politehnica of Bucharest, as the volume of contribution increased on UPB's side and such changes were required -> first chapter.

results.resultTitle: O8-EN-Advanced IoT applications: security and privacy topics
results.resultDescription: This output consists of a 25 pages chapter that deals with security and privacy in the Internet of Things system technology. The chapter present important security threats and mitigation in IoT systems and guides the reader through the basic operations required to secure any IoT device. Considering how vast the security field is, the purpose of this chapter is to raise awareness about the importance of securing Internet of Things systems and to encourage the readers to explore this area further on. Here, 39 working days belonging to the O8 work load have been transferred from Wyliodrin to the University Politehnica of Bucharest, as the volume of contribution increased on UPB's side and such changes were required.

results.resultTitle: O1 Analysis of target group needs
results.resultDescription:
The main purpose of it was to uncover the real potential training system users needs in the field of OSH training content and the functionality
of the training system as well as to review, collect and compare the legislative regulations in the field of OSH in project partners countries. The results of this survey are collected in the document 'Applicable legislation in the field of OSH European Report'. The general analysis of all collected feedback from case-studies and the general questionnaire are composed to the main document 'O1: Analysis of target groups’ needs European Report'.
The results of this analysis was directly used to support the development of: O2 training materials, O3 methodology and O4 Dedicated ICT Portal. Although the research was carried out mainly for the purposes of the SPOSH project, knowledge and conclusions from this analysis can be successfully used for other purposes, e.g. statistical, not only
for the development and creation of a training system.
results.resultCategory: Research material bringing forward the reflection in the sector

results.resultTitle: O3 Common learning methodology including assessment strategy EN
results.resultDescription:
This product is another basic product of the project and provides input to the development and integration of the platform. The methodology was developed to combine new teaching methods, including classical teaching, e-learning and blended learning. The SPOSH methodology present all stages of the training and provide guidance and information on how to complete and achieve them.
Common learning methodology including assessment strategy will be form of guidelines for advanced portal users teachers, consultants, portal administrators. Common learning methodology will contain: - pedagogic concept, - portal use guidelines, - example use cases of portal use, - defined learning objectives, - scenarios for utilization of ECVET system, - peer-learning methods, - work-based VET training activities description, -
assessment and validation strategy allowing to evaluation learning process with utilization of SPOSH platform functionality.
results.resultCategory: Practical & reusable resources for the practitioners

results.resultDescription:
This in result in combination with the results O2 and O3 constitute one coherent product. 
The system was built based on the results of research conducted as part of the intellectual output O1. The final shape of the system was achieved thanks to the recommendations contained in the methodology (O3). The platform offers controlled access to educational materials, but primarily is an open environment enabling users' knowledge exchange, peer learning, synchronous and asynchronous interaction with other users. The platform has the ability to monitor and assess the progress of users, the ability to exchange ideas of users and knowledge through rich communication systems (for example: text messages, voice communication, forums, virtual classrooms, visual communication); support for training activities in the field of vocational education and training and learning at work.
System is available on-line at www.sposh-course.piap.pl

results.resultTitle: Output 1- Analysis of target groups needs(SVK)
results.resultDescription: In appendix is a report D1 from works realized in output 1 in Slovak language. The aim of this deliverable or outcome were performing an in-depth analysis and identifying target groups' needs and requirements. The deliverable contains two parts, namely an analysis of engineering companies' needs concerning the employees being hired, i.e. the graduates of secondary vocational schools and an analysis of secondary teachers' needs concerning their education in the field of robotics.  Analyses were prepared in all the partner countries and all the project partners were involved. These were evaluated for each of the countries individually and as a whole.

results.resultTitle: Output 2- Set of training materials from the field of robotics(SVK)
results.resultDescription:
In appendix is a report D2 from works realized in output 2 in Slovak language. Educational materials (lessons) on the basis of which the training-based ICT platform are based on the project based on two areas:

 -Industrial robotics - basic terms and definition including parameters, programming, safety of robotic systems, visual and camera systems for robots, robotic end effectors, sensorial equipment for industrial robots.

 -Service robotics - basic terms and definition including parameters, programming, wheeled service robots, tracked service robots, robotic end effectors, walking service robots, climbing service robots, sensor equipment for service robots, multi-agent and swam systems, development trends in service robotics area.

results.resultTitle: Output 3- ICT platform for secondary school teachers in field of robotics(SVK)
results.resultDescription:
In appendix is a report D3 from works realized in output 3 in Slovak language.The ICT training platform for the training of secondary vocational school teachers in the field of robotics is developed on the basis of educational materials - lessons. It is developed on the basis of on-line training of target
groups, e-learning, so it is available to users according to time and space unlimited. The educational and training
ICT platform is the main intellectual output of the RUSOS project. A virtual models is also part of the ICT
platform, which serve to verify the knowledge gained in the learning ICT platform. The virtual models are created in virtual reality and consists of examples 3D models of different robots and other automated devices.

A research report containing list of areas of interest in which ethical skills need to be developed. Once identified, the areas of interest will serve as a basis of several lists of ethical topics to be realized in each area. Each topic will correspond to a required skill. These topics will have to
be faced during the training course format that will characterize the training units in the final catalogue.

Definition of the training format characterized by a non-formal part to be attended in classroom, to
introduce ethical topics to trainees, and a second part that has to be developed in an outdoor modality in venues with high difficulties and characterized by high levels of poverty,
or discrimination for people, inside development projects carried out by ngos. In this way the non-formal session can be linked to different contexts of outdoor training
experience, because the non-formal session will have the aim to introduce topics and problems and will work as a reflective module.

results.resultTitle: Guideline document for planning HECOS FOR ETHICS training experiences
results.resultDescription:
guideline document, articulated in three different
sections, aimed at
- helping training companies to identify company needs and the training aims, and choosing
the most appropriate methodology and schedule to hit the training aims;
- helping training providers and ngos to design a HECOS FOR ETHICS training experience
- helping NGOS to organize the informal training and choose the most appropriate venue to
develop it.

The catalogue presents several units, linked to the training aims and the venues where the training activity could be developed. The catalogue describes modalities to assess final skills to include them into the EQF. For every training event the training centre will also be presented together with the ngo that will carry out the training activity and the solidarity projects in each venue where the course will be realized. Every company is also be able to
choose the most appropriate course, to be developed in the most appropriate venue depending on the vocation of their CSR policy.
The catalogue is illustrated with pictures of the venues, the curricula of the involved ngos and training centres and the description of the cooperation projects developed in those
venues by ngos.

Training course schedules of the catalogue and related training experiences and aims integrated in higher education studies and curricula. The Academic group
of the project ( the three universities ) has applied the ECTS frame to integrate the learning outcomes in their academic curricula. In particular the ODISEE UNiversity has design a test framework to acknowledge the learning results and decline them in ects credits.

promo and advertising activities
have been planned following a bottom-up approach: each partner has proposed its
own set of activities trying to maximise the added value of its existing network, database
of contacts, consolidated communication tools and channels with project stakeholders.
Partners of the same country/region coordinated themselves in order to make activities
more efficient, avoiding duplication and possible conflicts in communication actions
addressing the same target audiences. AICCRE Veneto facilitated the integration in
partners’ plans of common tools, in particular the link between the project website and
the webpages dedicated to the project developed in the official partners’ websites.
Moreover, AICCRE Veneto coordinated the monitoring of the activities, promoting
exchange of practices and tools among the partners

Set of info and promo actions and events involving Local and National Authorities in order to promote the adoption
of the concept in new local and international contexts

Document for internal use describing activities, cost, responsibilities and strategies to be
activated to:
- guarantee the availability and update of the implementation of the training courses
included in the catalogue;
- guarantee the continuation of the HECOS FOR ETHICS website for at least three years after
the project’s lifespan
The pricing policy to be adopted after the project lifespan to propose on the training market
the training experiences defined by the project will specify:
- HECOS FOR ETHICS services’ prices and costs,
- enrollment and payment modalities,
- any other issue that can guarantee new resources to enhance the sustainability of the
project
- quality standards to build a HECOS FOR ETHICS Ngos roster.
